## Problem

`bin/shellspec-format` runs under `set -e` (line 5). At line 213 it increments the indent with `((indent_level++))` as a standalone command. Bash's `((expr))` exits non-zero when the arithmetic result is 0, and post-increment evaluates to the *old* value. The first block keyword in any file therefore evaluates `((0++))` -> result 0 -> exit status 1 -> errexit terminates the script mid-stream.

The file-processing path at line 292 happens to survive because `if format_shellspec <"$file" >"$temp_file"; then` suppresses errexit for the whole condition, including inside the called function. The stdin path at line 285 calls `format_shellspec` bare, so it dies.

## Evidence

Minimal repro of the mechanism:

    $ bash -c 'set -e; i=0; ((i++)); echo "survived, i=$i"'; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

The documented primary usage (`shellspec-format < input > output`, README/usage lines 32 and 36):

    $ printf 'Describe "x"\nIt "y"\nEnd\nEnd\n' | ./bin/shellspec-format; echo "exit=$?"
    Describe "x"
    exit=1

One line of seven is emitted. The same defect makes `tests/bin_format_spec.sh` fail its very first case:

    [BIN-TEST] Testing Basic block indentation
    [FAIL] Basic block indentation formatting command failed

Same construct, same bug, at `bin/shellspec-format:192`: `((indent_level > 0)) && ((indent_level--))` is safe only because errexit exempts commands inside an `&&` list.

## Impact

The standalone formatter is unusable in its documented pipe mode: it silently truncates output to the first line and exits 1. Anyone using `cat file | shellspec-format > file.new` loses the file's contents. `make test-bin` fails, and because `tests/run_tests.sh` checks the bin suite's exit code, `make test` currently fails outright.

## Fix

Replace the bare arithmetic command with one whose exit status does not depend on the value. At line 213:

    indent_level=$((indent_level + 1))

and at line 192:

    if ((indent_level > 0)); then indent_level=$((indent_level - 1)); fi

Then add a regression case to `tests/bin_format_spec.sh` that pipes multi-line input through stdin and asserts the full line count comes back.

## Resolution
indent_level=$((x+1)) replaces ((x++)); stdin mode emits all lines. Regression test added to bin_format_spec.sh.
title: set -e plus ((indent_level++)) aborts stdin mode after the first block keyword

body:
## Problem

All three formatter implementations apply the current block indentation to the HEREDOC terminator line:

- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:219` — `make_indent(indent_level) .. trimmed`
- `bin/shellspec-format:224` — `printf "%s%s\n" "$(make_indent $indent_level)" "$trimmed"`
- `autoload/shellspec.vim:116` — `repeat('  ', l:indent) . l:trimmed`

For a plain `<<EOF` heredoc the shell requires the terminator at column 0; only `<<-` permits leading whitespace, and even then only tabs. Indenting it means the shell never finds the delimiter and swallows the remainder of the file as heredoc body.

## Evidence

Input (valid shell):

    Describe "x"
    It "y"
    When call cat <<EOF
    hello
    EOF
    The output should equal "hello"
    End
    End

After `./bin/shellspec-format file.spec.sh` (identical output from the Lua path):

    Describe "x"$
      It "y"$
        When call cat <<EOF$
    hello$
        EOF$
      End$
    End$

Running the result:

    $ bash f.sh
    f.sh: line 8: warning: here-document at line 3 delimited by end-of-file (wanted `EOF')

Every line after the terminator — the assertion and both `End`s — is now heredoc body rather than spec code.

The behaviour is asserted as correct by the test suite, which is why it survived: `tests/format_spec.lua:155` expects `"    EOF"`, and `tests/golden_master_test.sh:158,165,172` expect `      EOF`, `      DATA`, `      SCRIPT`.

## Impact

Running `:ShellSpecFormat` on any spec file containing a HEREDOC silently converts working shell into a script whose assertions no longer execute. With `auto_format = true` (the configuration the README recommends) this happens on every save, with no error shown. This is data corruption of the user's source file.

## Fix

Emit the terminator with its original text and no added indentation — the same treatment the heredoc body already gets:

    -- lua/shellspec/format.lua
    if is_heredoc_end(line, heredoc_delimiter) then
      state = State.NORMAL
      heredoc_delimiter = nil
      table.insert(result, line)   -- was: make_indent(indent_level) .. trimmed
    end

Apply the equivalent change at `bin/shellspec-format:224` (`echo "$line"`) and `autoload/shellspec.vim:116` (`call add(l:result, l:line)`).

If `<<-` support is wanted later, track whether the opener used `<<-` and only then re-indent, with tabs. Update the now-wrong expectations in `tests/format_spec.lua:155` and `tests/golden_master_test.sh:158,165,172`, and add a case that pipes the formatted output through `bash -n` plus a grep for the end-of-file warning so the regression cannot return.

## Resolution
HEREDOC terminator emitted verbatim in all three implementations; bash -n clean, no end-of-file warning. Test expectations corrected in format_spec.lua, golden_master_test.sh, bin_format_spec.sh.
title: Formatter indents HEREDOC terminators, producing shell that never closes the heredoc

## Problem

All three shell test suites set `set -e` and count passes with `((TESTS_PASSED++))` as the last command of `print_pass()`. Post-increment from 0 yields arithmetic result 0, so `(( ))` returns exit status 1, the function returns 1, and errexit terminates the suite. The first test that *passes* kills the run.

## Evidence

    $ ./tests/integration_test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
    Running nvim-shellspec integration tests...
    [TEST] Neovim version compatibility
    [PASS] Neovim v0.12.5 >= 0.7.0
    exit=1

1 of 8 tests ran. Same for golden master:

    $ ./tests/golden_master_test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
    [GOLDEN] Testing basic_nesting
    [PASS] basic_nesting formatting matches expected output
    exit=1

1 of 3 cases ran. `print_summary` is never reached in either suite, so the "Passed/Failed/Total" report never prints.

This is the true cause of the excuse recorded in `tests/run_tests.sh:89` and `:106`: "This is a known issue with test environment nvim interaction". It is not an nvim interaction issue; it is an arithmetic-expansion exit status.

## Impact

Seven of eight integration tests and two of three golden-master cases have never executed. Among the tests that never run is integration Test 7, the health check — which would have caught the `vim.health.report_start` removal that breaks `:checkhealth shellspec` on Neovim 0.12. The suites report nothing and are treated as infrastructure flakiness rather than as a defect.

## Fix

Use a form whose exit status is unconditional. In each of the three files:

    print_pass() {
      echo -e "${GREEN}[PASS]${NC} $1"
      TESTS_PASSED=$((TESTS_PASSED + 1))
    }

and the same for `print_fail`/`TESTS_FAILED` (`tests/integration_test.sh:29`, `tests/golden_master_test.sh:29`, `tests/bin_format_spec.sh:38`) — `TESTS_FAILED` hits the same zero-value case on the first failure.

After fixing, run all three suites and expect real failures to surface; do not re-suppress them.

## Resolution
All counters use $((x+1)); integration runs 10/10, golden 3/3, bin 16/16.
title: ((TESTS_PASSED++)) under set -e aborts every shell test suite after its first passing assertion

## Problem

The runner executes the integration and golden-master suites with output discarded, then sets the result variable to `true` in *both* branches:

    if timeout 30 ./tests/integration_test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      INTEGRATION_PASSED=true
    else
      echo "This is a known issue with test environment nvim interaction"
      INTEGRATION_PASSED=true  # Mark as passed since core functionality works
    fi

Identical structure at lines 101-109 for `GOLDEN_PASSED`. The final gate at line 150 then reads variables that can only ever be `true`.

## Evidence

`tests/run_tests.sh:91` — `INTEGRATION_PASSED=true # Mark as passed since core functionality works`
`tests/run_tests.sh:108` — `GOLDEN_PASSED=true # Mark as passed since core functionality works`

Both suites currently exit 1 after their first assertion (see the `((TESTS_PASSED++))` finding), and `make test` still prints:

    ✓ Integration Tests: PASSED
    ✓ Golden Master Tests: PASSED

`>/dev/null 2>&1` additionally discards the diff output that `golden_master_test.sh:219-227` produces on mismatch, so even a genuine formatting regression leaves no trace.

## Impact

Two of the four suites are decorative. A formatting regression that breaks every golden-master case reports green. The comment "core functionality works" is an assertion by fiat that the suite exists to check — the gate was removed rather than the failure fixed.

## Fix

Let the exit status decide, and keep the output:

    if timeout 30 ./tests/integration_test.sh; then
      INTEGRATION_PASSED=true
    else
      INTEGRATION_PASSED=false
    fi

Same for the golden-master block. Both suites already have the `run_test_suite "script"` helper that does exactly this — route them through it (`run_test_suite "Integration Tests" "script" "./tests/integration_test.sh" INTEGRATION_PASSED`) rather than duplicating the inline form. If a suite is genuinely too slow or environment-dependent for the default run, gate it behind an opt-out flag and print that it was skipped; never report a skipped suite as passed.

## Resolution
Both suites routed through run_test_suite and gated on real exit status; output no longer discarded.
title: run_tests.sh hardcodes the integration and golden-master suites to PASSED on failure

## Problem

Both health implementations call the `vim.health.report_start` / `report_ok` / `report_info` / `report_warn` / `report_error` family. That API was deprecated in Neovim 0.10 in favour of `vim.health.start` / `ok` / `info` / `warn` / `error`, and has since been removed. On Neovim 0.12 the fields are `nil`, so the very first call raises.

## Evidence

On NVIM v0.12.5:

    health.report_start exists: false
    health.start exists: true
    health.check ok=false err=.../lua/shellspec/health.lua:7: attempt to call field 'report_start' (a nil value)
    init.health ok=false err=.../lua/shellspec/init.lua:52: attempt to call field 'report_start' (a nil value)

`:checkhealth shellspec` therefore reports an error instead of a health report. Integration test 7 (`tests/integration_test.sh:201`) exists precisely to catch this, but never runs — the suite aborts at test 1.

## Impact

`:checkhealth shellspec`, the plugin's only self-diagnostic and the first thing a user runs when the plugin misbehaves, is broken on every currently supported Neovim. The failure is a Lua traceback, which reads as "the plugin is broken" rather than "the health check is out of date".

## Fix

Switch to the current names in `lua/shellspec/health.lua` (lines 7, 12, 14, 20, 25-29, 32, 39, 41, 47, 49, 55, 62-65, 67-68, 82, 94, 96-97, 105, 107):

    local health = vim.health
    health.start("ShellSpec.nvim")
    health.ok(...)  health.info(...)  health.warn(...)  health.error(...)

Drop the `vim.health or require("health")` fallback: `require("health")` predates Neovim 0.7, which is already the declared floor.

Delete `M.health()` from `lua/shellspec/init.lua:49-79` outright — `:checkhealth shellspec` dispatches to `lua/shellspec/health.lua`'s `M.check`, nothing calls `init.health`, and keeping a second copy is what let this rot unnoticed in two places.

Fix the shell suites first (see the `((TESTS_PASSED++))` finding) so integration test 7 actually guards this going forward.

## Resolution
health.lua uses vim.health.start/ok/info/warn/error; duplicate init.lua M.health deleted. :checkhealth clean on 0.12.5.
title: checkhealth errors on Neovim 0.12: vim.health.report_* was removed

body:
## Problem

`M.format_selection` slices the requested lines out of the buffer and hands them to `M.format_lines`, which always starts at `indent_level = 0`. The surrounding block context is discarded, so any selection that does not begin at the top level is re-indented as if it were a whole file, while the lines outside the range keep their original indentation.

## Evidence

Buffer:

    1: [Describe "x"]
    2: [  Context "c"]
    3: [    It "y"]
    4: [      When call echo hi]
    5: [      The output should equal "hi"]
    6: [    End]
    7: [  End]
    8: [End]

After `format_selection(buf, 3, 5)`:

    1: [Describe "x"]
    2: [  Context "c"]
    3: [It "y"]
    4: [  When call echo hi]
    5: [  The output should equal "hi"]
    6: [    End]
    7: [  End]
    8: [End]

`It` moved from column 4 to column 0 and its body from 6 to 2, while the matching `End` on line 6 stayed at column 4.

The same path backs the `:ShellSpecFormatRange` command created at `lua/shellspec/init.lua:27` and `lua/shellspec/autocmds.lua:25`, and the visual-mode keybinding the README recommends at line 99.

`format_selection` also has no `pcall`, unlike `format_buffer` (`format.lua:237`), so a failure mid-way propagates as a raw error.

## Impact

The documented range-format command mangles indentation for every selection that is not at the top level — which is nearly every useful selection in a spec file. The damage is silent and spans lines the user did not select.

## Fix

Seed the state machine with the indentation already present at the start of the range, and let `format_lines` accept that seed:

    function M.format_lines(lines, start_indent)
      local indent_level = start_indent or 0
      ...

    function M.format_selection(bufnr, start_line, end_line)
      bufnr = bufnr or 0
      local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, start_line - 1, end_line, false)
      local first = lines[1] or ""
      local level = math.floor(#(first:match("^%s*") or "") / config.get("indent_size"))
      local formatted = M.format_lines(lines, level)
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(bufnr, start_line - 1, end_line, false, formatted)
    end

Wrap the body in `pcall` and surface failures via `vim.notify`, matching `format_buffer`. Add a unit test in `tests/format_spec.lua` that formats a nested sub-range and asserts the surrounding lines are untouched — there is currently no test for `format_selection` at all.

## Resolution
format_lines takes start_indent; format_selection seeds it from the first line's indent and is pcall-wrapped.
title: ShellSpecFormatRange re-indents a selection from level 0 and corrupts nested blocks

body:
## Problem

`detect_heredoc_start` searches the whole trimmed line for `<<` patterns with no anchoring and no awareness of shell context. Two consequences:

1. A here-string `<<<"word"` contains `<<"` starting at offset 1, so it matches the `<<"([^"]*)"` branch and yields `word` as a delimiter. Likewise `<<<EOF` matches the `<<[A-Z_]` branch.
2. The heredoc check runs *before* the comment check (`format.lua:170` vs `:189`), so a comment or string that merely names a heredoc starts heredoc state.

Once in heredoc state the formatter waits for a terminator line that never arrives, and passes every remaining line through unformatted.

## Evidence

Here-string, `bin/shellspec-format` (Lua path produces byte-identical output):

    input:                                   output:
    Describe "x"                             Describe "x"
    It "y"                                     It "y"
    When call grep foo <<<"$input"               When call grep foo <<<"$input"
    The status should be success             The status should be success     <- unformatted
    End                                      End                              <- unformatted
    End                                      End

Comment mentioning a heredoc:

    input:                                   output:
    Describe "x"                             Describe "x"
    # note: uses <<EOF here                    # note: uses <<EOF here
    It "y"                                   It "y"                           <- unformatted
    When call echo hi                        When call echo hi                <- unformatted
    End                                      End
    End                                      End

A related case: when a line is both a block keyword and a heredoc opener, the heredoc branch wins and the indent is never incremented, so the closing `End` misaligns:

    Describe "x"          ->   Describe "x"
    It "y" <<EOF                 It "y" <<EOF
    body                         body
    EOF                          EOF
    End                        End            <- should be indented one level
    End                        End

There is also an unterminated-state case: `<<''` matches `<<'([^']*)'` with an empty capture, and `is_heredoc_end` returns false for an empty delimiter (`format.lua:37`, `bin/shellspec-format:86`), so the formatter can never leave heredoc state.

## Impact

The formatter silently stops formatting from the offending line to end of file. There is no error and no notification — the user sees a partially formatted buffer and has no indication why. Here-strings and heredoc-mentioning comments are both ordinary content in shell specs.

## Fix

Anchor the detection so `<<<` and comments cannot match, and reorder the state machine:

1. Move the `is_comment` check above the heredoc check in all three implementations (`format.lua:189` before `:170`, `bin/shellspec-format:198` before `:182`, `autoload/shellspec.vim:82` before `:63`).
2. Require the redirection to be exactly two `<`: in Lua match against `"[^<]<<([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)"` plus a separate start-of-line case, or simpler, reject up front with `if trimmed:match("<<<") then return nil end`. In bash, add a guard `[[ $trimmed == *"<<<"* ]] && return 1` before the pattern loop.
3. Treat an empty capture as no match: `if delim == "" then return nil end`.
4. Detect the block keyword before taking the heredoc branch so `It "y" <<EOF` still increments the indent.

Add unit cases to `tests/format_spec.lua` for each of the four inputs above; none is covered today.

## Resolution
<<< rejected up front, comment check moved before HEREDOC check, empty delimiters rejected, block-keyword check runs first. All three implementations.
title: Here-strings and any line merely mentioning <<NAME are misdetected as HEREDOC starts

body:
## Problem

In-place mode writes to a `mktemp` file and then `mv`s it over the target:

    temp_file=$(mktemp)
    if format_shellspec <"$file" >"$temp_file"; then
      mv "$temp_file" "$file"

`mktemp` creates the file with mode 0600, and `mv` within a filesystem replaces the destination inode, carrying the temp file's mode with it. The original file's permissions are discarded.

## Evidence

    $ chmod 755 a.spec.sh; stat -c '%a' a.spec.sh
    755
    $ ./bin/shellspec-format a.spec.sh; stat -c '%a' a.spec.sh
    600

Spec files are routinely executable — the repo's own `test_example.spec.sh` is mode 100755, and `tests/*.sh` are 100755.

`mktemp` with no `TMPDIR` argument also places the temp file in `/tmp`, which is usually a different filesystem from the repo; `mv` then falls back to copy+unlink, which additionally breaks hard links and resets ownership when run as root.

## Impact

Formatting an executable spec file makes it non-executable, so `./my_spec.sh` and anything invoking it by path stops working. Group and other read access is removed too, which breaks shared checkouts and CI caches. The repo's own pre-commit hook `check-shebang-scripts-are-executable` would start failing on any file the formatter touched.

## Fix

Create the temp file next to the target and copy the original's mode onto it before the move:

    temp_file=$(mktemp "${file}.shellspec-format.XXXXXX")
    trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' EXIT INT TERM
    if format_shellspec <"$file" >"$temp_file"; then
      chmod --reference="$file" "$temp_file" 2>/dev/null || chmod "$(stat -c '%a' "$file")" "$temp_file"
      mv "$temp_file" "$file"

Creating it in the target directory also makes the `mv` atomic, so an interrupted run cannot leave a half-written spec file. The `trap` covers the leak noted separately — today an interrupt between `mktemp` and `mv` leaves the temp file behind.

## Resolution
Temp file created beside the target with chmod --reference before mv, plus a cleanup trap. Mode-preservation regression test added.
title: In-place formatting resets the file mode to 0600, stripping the executable bit

body:
## Problem

Three of the four HEREDOC patterns in `s:detect_heredoc_start` are single-quoted Vim strings; the second is double-quoted:

    let l:patterns = [
      \ '<<\([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\)',
      \ "<<'\([^']*\)'",
      \ '<<"\([^"]*\)"',
      \ '<<-\([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\)'
    \ ]

In a double-quoted Vim string an unrecognised escape drops the backslash, so `\(` and `\)` become literal `(` and `)`. The pattern that reaches `matchlist` is `<<'([^']*)'` — it looks for literal parentheses in the text and has no capture group.

## Evidence

    :let s:p = "<<'\([^']*\)'"
    :echo string(s:p)
    '<<''([^'']*)'''
    :echo string(matchlist("When call cat <<'EOF'", s:p))
    []

Consequence, via `shellspec#format_lines`:

    input                                  output
    Describe "x"                           Describe "x"
    It "y"                                   It "y"
    When call cat <<'EOF'                      When call cat <<'EOF'
    body                                       body            <- re-indented
    EOF                                        EOF             <- re-indented
    The output should equal "body"             The output should equal "body"
    End                                      End
    End                                    End

`body` and the `EOF` terminator were both indented; in the Lua path they would have been preserved verbatim.

`test_example.spec.sh:18` uses exactly this form (`When call cat <<'DATA'`), and the golden-master suite has a `<<'DATA'` case at `tests/golden_master_test.sh:137` — but that suite only exercises the Lua path and aborts before reaching the case.

## Impact

On Vim and pre-0.7 Neovim, quoted-HEREDOC content is re-indented rather than preserved — the exact behaviour the README advertises at line 47 ("Maintains original formatting within `<<EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, ..."). Content inside a `<<'EOF'` block is by definition literal data; re-indenting it changes what the spec asserts.

## Fix

Make the pattern a single-quoted string like its three siblings, escaping the embedded quote by doubling it:

    \ '<<''\([^'']*\)''',

Then add a VimScript-path test. The fallback implementation currently has zero test coverage of any kind, which is why a pure quoting mistake survived: `tests/integration_test.sh:208-217` only checks that `:ShellSpecFormat` exists under `vim`, never what it produces.

## Resolution
Pattern converted to a single-quoted Vim string with doubled quotes; VimScript fallback now detects <<'EOF'. Covered by parity_test.sh and integration test 8.
title: VimScript fallback never detects <<'EOF' — double-quoted string eats the regex group escapes

body:
## Problem

The repository has four workflows — `codeql.yml`, `pr-lint.yml`, `stale.yml`, `sync-labels.yml`. None invokes `make test`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, or any individual suite. `codeql.yml` analyses only `language: ["actions"]`, i.e. the workflow files themselves. The `Makefile` defines a `ci` target (`ci: check test lint`, line 262) that nothing calls.

## Evidence

    $ grep -rn 'run_tests\|make test\|make ci\|nvim' .github/workflows/
    (no matches)

Workflow steps in full: `codeql.yml:30-34` (CodeQL on `actions`), `pr-lint.yml:28-30` (`ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint`), `stale.yml:26`, `sync-labels.yml:36-41`. No checkout-plus-test job exists.

The gap is load-bearing here: three separate defects found in this audit are exactly what a CI test run would have caught — the shell suites aborting after one assertion, `make test-bin` failing, and `:checkhealth` erroring on current Neovim.

## Impact

Nothing verifies plugin behaviour on any pull request. `make test` fails on the current `main` and no signal reaches GitHub. The four test suites, the Makefile `ci` target, and the README's testing section describe a verification story that is never executed outside a developer's terminal.

## Fix

Add `.github/workflows/test.yml` running on `push`/`pull_request` to `main`, with a Neovim version matrix covering the declared floor and current stable:

    ---
    name: Test
    on:
      push: { branches: [main] }
      pull_request: { branches: [main] }
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        permissions: { contents: read }
        strategy:
          fail-fast: false
          matrix:
            nvim: ["v0.7.2", "stable"]
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@<pinned-sha>  # pin as the other workflows do
          - uses: rhysd/action-setup-vim@<pinned-sha>
            with: { neovim: true, version: "${{ matrix.nvim }}" }
          - run: make test

Pin every action to a commit SHA with a version comment, matching the convention already used in `codeql.yml:31` and `sync-labels.yml:37`.

Fix the suites first — `make test` fails today, so adding this workflow before the `((TESTS_PASSED++))` and `bin/shellspec-format` fixes lands a red main branch.

## Resolution
Added .github/workflows/test.yml running make test on a Neovim v0.7.2/stable matrix; actions pinned to verified SHAs.
title: No CI workflow runs the test suite

body:
## Problem

The README advertises detection for `*_spec.sh`, `*.spec.sh`, `spec/*.sh`, `test/*.sh`, and "files in nested `spec/` directories". Only the first two work.

Vim matches an autocmd pattern against the full (absolute) path as soon as the pattern contains a `/`. `spec/*.sh` and `test/*.sh` therefore only match a buffer whose entire path is literally `spec/foo.sh` — never true for a real file. The Lua `"**/spec/**/*.sh"` pattern at `autocmds.lua:97` does not match a file sitting directly in a `spec/` directory either.

## Evidence

    proj/spec/plain.sh  -> filetype=''
    proj/test/plain.sh  -> filetype=''
    proj/x_spec.sh      -> filetype='shellspec'

measured by opening each file with the plugin sourced (`nvim --headless -u NONE -c 'set rtp+=…' -c 'source plugin/shellspec.vim' -c 'edit <file>'`).

Patterns declared: `ftdetect/shellspec.vim:4-5` and `lua/shellspec/autocmds.lua:84-85` (`"spec/*.sh"`, `"test/*.sh"`), `autocmds.lua:97` (`"**/spec/**/*.sh"`).

README claims affected: line 40 and lines 62-66.

## Impact

A project that follows the ShellSpec convention of putting specs in `spec/` gets no syntax highlighting, no indentation, no commands and no formatting — the plugin appears not to work at all, while the README says that layout is supported. Users following the lazy.nvim snippet at README line 12 (`ft = "shellspec"`) additionally never load the plugin in that case, because the filetype is never set.

## Fix

Use patterns that match against the tail of the path. In `ftdetect/shellspec.vim`:

    autocmd BufRead,BufNewFile */spec/*.sh setfiletype shellspec
    autocmd BufRead,BufNewFile */test/*.sh setfiletype shellspec

A leading `*/` makes the pattern match any path ending in `spec/<name>.sh`. For arbitrary nesting below `spec/`, add `*/spec/**.sh`.

Prefer declaring all of this once via `vim.filetype.add({ pattern = { … } })` in the Lua path rather than maintaining two divergent copies (see the duplicate-detection finding).

Before shipping the fix, decide whether `test/*.sh` should match at all: it claims every `.sh` file under any `test/` directory, most of which are ordinary shell scripts, not ShellSpec specs. Scoping that to `*/test/*_spec.sh` would be safer. Whichever way it goes, make the README match the implementation.

Add integration cases asserting the resulting filetype for `spec/foo.sh`, `test/foo.sh`, and a nested `spec/unit/foo.sh` — none is covered today.

## Resolution
Patterns changed to */spec/*.sh and */spec/**/*.sh; test/*.sh dropped as over-broad. README and doc/ updated to match.
title: Three of the four documented filetype patterns never fire

## Problem

The `clean` target runs unscoped `find` deletions outside the repository:

    find . -name "*.bak" -delete
    find . -name "*.tmp" -delete
    find /tmp -name "*shellspec*" -delete 2>/dev/null || true
    find /var/folders -name "*shellspec*" -delete 2>/dev/null || true

`/tmp` and `/var/folders` are shared, machine-wide directories. The glob `*shellspec*` matches anything any process on the machine happens to have named that way — another checkout's build artefacts, a running ShellSpec test run's scratch directory, an editor swap file, another user's files where permissions allow. `2>/dev/null || true` suppresses every error, so the target reports success regardless of what it touched or failed to touch.

## Evidence

`Makefile:241-244`, quoted above. The target is advertised in `make help` as "Remove temporary files and test artifacts".

That the repo's own tests create such files is what makes this live rather than theoretical: `tests/integration_test.sh:96` uses `mktemp -t "shellspec_test_XXXXXX.spec.sh"` and `tests/golden_master_test.sh:195-197` creates three more per case, all in `/tmp` and all matching `*shellspec*`. A `make clean` run concurrently with `make test` deletes the running suite's fixtures.

`find . -name "*.bak" -delete` is unscoped within the repo as well — it recurses into any working directory the user happens to have nested there.

## Impact

A routine housekeeping command can delete files it does not own, outside the project, with no record of what it removed. On a shared machine it reaches other users' temp files. Concurrent test runs are corrupted. Nothing in the target's name or help text warns of scope beyond the repository.

## Fix

Scope the deletions to the repository and let the tests clean up after themselves:

    .PHONY: clean
    clean: ## Remove temporary files and test artifacts
    	@echo "$(BLUE)Cleaning temporary files...$(NC)"
    	find . -path ./.git -prune -o -name '*.bak' -type f -print -delete
    	find . -path ./.git -prune -o -name '*.tmp' -type f -print -delete
    	@echo "  ✓ Cleaned temporary files"

Drop the `/tmp` and `/var/folders` lines entirely. The test suites already `rm -f` their own temp files (`integration_test.sh:103,148,197`, `golden_master_test.sh:234`); make that reliable by adding `trap 'rm -f "$TEST_FILE" "$EXPECTED_FILE"' EXIT INT TERM` so an interrupted run does not leave residue that a system-wide sweep is then invented to handle.

Keep `-print` so the target reports what it deleted instead of doing it silently.

## Resolution
clean scoped to the repository with -path ./.git -prune; the /tmp and /var/folders sweeps are gone. Suites clean up via traps instead.
title: make clean deletes files system-wide from /tmp and /var/folders

body:
## Problem

The release target rewrites the version in `bin/shellspec-format` with an over-broad substitution:

    sed -i.bak "s/shellspec-format [0-9.]*/shellspec-format $$new_version/" $(VERSION_BIN)

`[0-9.]*` matches the empty string, so the pattern matches `shellspec-format ` anywhere in the file — including the usage text and the examples, not just the `version()` function it was meant to update. Each match gets a version number spliced in.

## Evidence

The damage is committed. `bin/shellspec-format:20`:

    Usage: shellspec-format 2.0.2[OPTIONS] [FILE...]

and lines 36-38:

    shellspec-format 2.0.2< input.spec.sh > output.spec.sh
    shellspec-format 2.0.2file1.spec.sh file2.spec.sh
    cat file.spec.sh | shellspec-format 2.0.2--indent-size 4 --tabs

Every example in `--help` is now unrunnable as printed. The intended target, `bin/shellspec-format:44` (`echo "shellspec-format 2.0.2"`), is the only line that should have matched.

The rule re-applies on every release, so the corruption persists (the injected `2.0.2` is itself matched by `[0-9.]*` and replaced with the next version).

## Impact

`shellspec-format --help` prints a usage line and three examples that cannot be copied and run. The mismatch also misleads anyone reading the script for the invocation form.

## Fix

Anchor the substitution to the single line it is meant to change, matching the quoted form that `version-check` already greps for at `Makefile:62`:

    sed -i.bak "s/^  echo \"shellspec-format [0-9.]*\"/  echo \"shellspec-format $$new_version\"/" $(VERSION_BIN)

Then repair the committed text in `bin/shellspec-format`:

    Usage: shellspec-format [OPTIONS] [FILE...]
    ...
      shellspec-format < input.spec.sh > output.spec.sh
      shellspec-format file1.spec.sh file2.spec.sh
      cat file.spec.sh | shellspec-format --indent-size 4 --tabs

The same over-broad shape is worth checking in the sibling rules at `Makefile:213-214`; both are anchored to a distinctive assignment and are safe as written.

## Resolution
Release sed anchored to the version() echo line; help text and examples repaired in bin/shellspec-format.
title: Release sed corrupts the formatter's --help text on every version bump

## Problem

Four documented settings have no effect, and one advertised feature is unreachable:

- `heredoc_patterns` (README:85-90, config.lua:14-19) — read only by `get_heredoc_patterns()` at format.lua:13, which nothing calls. `detect_heredoc_start` hardcodes the four patterns at format.lua:22-29, so customising the option changes nothing.
- `preserve_empty_lines` (README:93, config.lua:25) — never read anywhere.
- `max_line_length` (README:94, config.lua:26) — never read anywhere.
- "⚡ Async formatting to prevent blocking (Neovim 0.7+)" (README:42) — `M.format_buffer_async` exists at format.lua:271 but no command, autocmd or export reaches it.

## Evidence

Repository-wide grep, excluding `.serena/`:

    heredoc_patterns      README.md:85  config.lua:14  format.lua:13,14
    preserve_empty_lines  README.md:93  config.lua:25
    max_line_length       README.md:94  config.lua:26
    get_heredoc_patterns  format.lua:13                       (definition only)
    format_buffer_async   format.lua:271                      (definition only)

Every hit is either the declaration, the README, or the dead accessor. There is no call site for any of them.

Two more declarations in the same class: `State.IN_DATA_BLOCK` (format.lua:9) is never compared against, and `M.format_buffer_compat` / `M.format_selection_compat` (init.lua:82,86), commented "Backward compatibility function for VimScript", are unreferenced — the VimScript path calls `autoload/shellspec.vim` instead.

## Impact

A user who customises `heredoc_patterns` to support a project-specific delimiter gets silence: no error, no warning, and no behaviour change. `setup()` accepts the keys because `vim.tbl_deep_extend` merges anything. The async claim sets an expectation about blocking behaviour on large buffers that the plugin does not meet — `format_buffer` is fully synchronous.

## Fix

Pick one direction per option rather than leaving the gap:

Wire it up — `detect_heredoc_start` should iterate `get_heredoc_patterns()` instead of hardcoding, deriving the capture from each configured pattern. This is the only one of the four with a plausible use.

Delete the rest — remove `preserve_empty_lines` and `max_line_length` from `config.lua:25-26` and README:93-94, remove `State.IN_DATA_BLOCK`, `M.format_buffer_compat`, `M.format_selection_compat`.

For async, either wire `format_buffer_async` to a command (`:ShellSpecFormatAsync`) and to the `BufWritePre` auto-format path at `autocmds.lua:71`, or drop the README:42 bullet. Note that as written it only defers the same synchronous work by one event-loop tick via `vim.schedule` — it does not make formatting non-blocking, so the bullet would overstate it even once wired.

Add a `setup()` guard that warns on unknown keys, so the next documented-but-unread option surfaces immediately:

    for k in pairs(opts or {}) do
      if M.defaults[k] == nil then
        vim.notify("shellspec: unknown option '" .. k .. "'", vim.log.levels.WARN)
      end
    end

## Resolution
heredoc_patterns wired into detect_heredoc_start and covered by a test; preserve_empty_lines and max_line_length removed; format_buffer_async wired to :ShellSpecFormatAsync; setup() warns on unknown keys.
title: README documents four configuration options and a feature that the code never reads or wires up

## Problem

The augroup is created once, at module load:

    -- autocmds.lua:7
    local augroup = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("ShellSpec", { clear = true })

`M.setup()` then appends autocmds to it without clearing. `plugin/shellspec.vim:24` calls `require('shellspec.autocmds').setup()` at startup, and `require("shellspec").setup(opts)` — the call the README's lazy.nvim snippet makes at line 14 — calls it again via `init.lua:20`. Nothing de-duplicates, because `{ clear = true }` ran before either call.

`init.lua:23-32` additionally re-creates the two global user commands that `autocmds.setup()` has just created at lines 41-50, and `init.lua:35-37` calls `autocmds.refresh()` when `auto_format` is set — a third registration pass, despite `setup()` already handling `auto_format` at line 63.

## Evidence

After plugin load plus two `setup()` calls:

    autocmds in group ShellSpec: 33
      24x  Detect ShellSpec files
       6x  Detect ShellSpec files in nested spec directories
       3x  Setup ShellSpec buffer

One registration pass produces 8 + 2 + 1 = 11 entries; three passes produce 33. A user following the README gets two passes, so `setup_buffer` runs twice on every `FileType shellspec` event, re-setting four buffer options and re-creating both buffer-local commands.

## Impact

Every ShellSpec buffer opened does its setup work N times, where N grows with each `setup()` call. With `auto_format = true` the `BufWritePre` handler is registered on each pass, so saving one file runs the whole formatter two or more times in sequence — each pass re-reading and rewriting the buffer. `M.cleanup()` clears the group wholesale, so a caller who registered once cannot remove just their own registration.

## Fix

Create the augroup inside `setup()` so each call clears the previous registration:

    -- autocmds.lua
    local augroup  -- created per setup()

    function M.setup()
      augroup = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("ShellSpec", { clear = true })
      ...
    end

    function M.cleanup()
      if augroup then vim.api.nvim_clear_autocmds({ group = augroup }) end
    end

`M.refresh()` then reduces to `M.setup()` and the `cleanup()` call in it becomes redundant.

Delete the duplicated command creation at `init.lua:23-32` — `autocmds.setup()` already creates both — and delete the `auto_format` branch at `init.lua:35-37`, since `autocmds.setup()` reads the same flag at line 63 after `config.setup(opts)` has run.

Drop `require('shellspec.config').setup()` from `plugin/shellspec.vim:21`: `config.lua:49` already calls `M.setup()` at module load.

## Resolution
Augroup created inside setup() with clear=true; duplicate command registration and the redundant auto_format branch removed from init.lua. Idempotent: 9 autocmds after one pass or two.
title: Following the README's setup() snippet registers every autocmd and command twice

body:
## Problem

The indent-increment tests in `shellspec#format_lines` anchor only at the start of the line and never require a following space or end-of-line:

    if l:trimmed =~ '^\(Describe\|Context\|ExampleGroup\|It\|Specify\|Example\)'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\([xf]\)\(Describe\|…\)'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(Data\|Parameters\)\s*$'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(BeforeEach\|AfterEach\|BeforeAll\|AfterAll\|Before\|After\)'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(BeforeCall\|AfterCall\|BeforeRun\|AfterRun\)'

Any line whose first characters happen to spell a keyword opens a block. The Lua and bash implementations get this right — `format.lua:55-60` requires `%s`, `bin/shellspec-format:98` requires `[[:space:]]`, and both require `\s*$` for the standalone hooks.

## Evidence

    :echo shellspec#format_lines(['Describe "x"', 'Items=3', 'Included stuff', 'End'])
    ['Describe "x"', '  Items=3', '    Included stuff', '  End']

`Items=3` matched `^…It…` and `Included stuff` matched `^…I…`? No — `Included` matches nothing, but by then `Items=3` had already incremented the indent, so `Included stuff` inherits level 2 and the closing `End` lands at level 1 instead of 0.

Ordinary shell assignments and commands that trip this: `Items=3`, `Examples=()`, `Contextual_setup`, `Beforehand=1`, `Afterwards`. The standalone-hook branches also match `Before some_arg` and `After cleanup`, which the other two implementations deliberately exclude by requiring end-of-line.

## Impact

On Vim and pre-0.7 Neovim, a spec containing any such line silently gains indentation levels that are never closed, cascading misindentation through the rest of the file. The three formatter implementations disagree about what a block keyword is, so the same file formats differently depending on the editor.

## Fix

Mirror the Lua implementation's anchoring:

    if l:trimmed =~ '^\(Describe\|Context\|ExampleGroup\|It\|Specify\|Example\)\s'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^[xf]\(Describe\|Context\|ExampleGroup\|It\|Specify\|Example\)\s'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(Data\|Parameters\)\s*$'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(BeforeEach\|AfterEach\|BeforeAll\|AfterAll\|Before\|After\)\s*$'
    elseif l:trimmed =~ '^\(BeforeCall\|AfterCall\|BeforeRun\|AfterRun\)\s*$'

The same unanchored shape appears in `indent/shellspec.vim:25,30,40` — fix those together, and note that `indent/shellspec.vim:40` uses `^\s*Parameters` where line 35 correctly uses `^\s*Data\s*$`.

The deeper problem is three hand-maintained copies of one keyword list drifting apart. Consider generating the VimScript patterns from a single declared list, or at minimum add a test that runs the same input through all three implementations and asserts identical output — no such cross-implementation test exists.

## Resolution
Block-keyword patterns anchored (\s after keywords, \s*$ after standalone hooks) in autoload and indent; parity test guards against future drift.
title: VimScript fallback block-keyword patterns are unanchored and match ordinary lines

body:
## Problem

Two buffer-setup lines act outside the buffer they are given:

    -- autocmds.lua:18
    vim.api.nvim_set_option_value("foldmethod", "indent", { win = 0 })

`win = 0` means the *current* window. A `FileType` autocmd fires whenever the filetype is set, which includes buffers loaded in the background (`:bufdo`, `:badd`, a plugin loading a file, a quickfix jump that has not switched windows yet). The option lands on whatever window happens to be current, not on the one showing `args.buf`.

    -- autocmds.lua:34
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_option(bufnr, "formatexpr", 'v:lua.require("shellspec.format").format_buffer()')

`formatexpr` is invoked for a *range*, with `v:lnum` and `v:count` naming it, and must return non-zero to fall back to internal formatting. This expression ignores both and reformats the entire buffer, then returns `nil`.

## Evidence

`lua/shellspec/autocmds.lua:18` and `:34`, quoted above.

The `formatexpr` consequence: `gqip` on one paragraph, or `gq` on a visual selection, rewrites every line in the buffer rather than the selected range — the same whole-buffer-vs-range confusion filed separately against `format_selection`, reached through a different entry point.

`nvim_buf_set_option` is also the deprecated form; every other option in this same function uses `nvim_set_option_value` (lines 12-15). It still resolves on 0.12.5 but emits a deprecation warning.

## Impact

Opening a spec file in the background can set `foldmethod=indent` on an unrelated window — the user sees folds appear in a file that has nothing to do with ShellSpec. And `gq`, a reflex keystroke, silently rewrites the whole buffer instead of the motion's range; on a file with a HEREDOC that compounds with the terminator-indentation defect.

## Fix

Scope the fold option to the windows actually displaying the buffer, and skip it when none does:

    for _, win in ipairs(vim.fn.win_findbuf(bufnr)) do
      vim.api.nvim_set_option_value("foldmethod", "indent", { win = win })
    end

Point `formatexpr` at a range-aware entry point and return 0 to signal the range was handled:

    vim.api.nvim_set_option_value("formatexpr", "v:lua.require'shellspec.format'.formatexpr()", { buf = bufnr })

    -- format.lua
    function M.formatexpr()
      M.format_selection(0, vim.v.lnum, vim.v.lnum + vim.v.count - 1)
      return 0
    end

This depends on `format_selection` preserving the surrounding indent level — fix that first, otherwise `gq` inherits the flattening bug.

Switch line 34 to `nvim_set_option_value` to match lines 12-15 and drop the `has('nvim-0.8')` guard: `nvim_set_option_value` exists from 0.8, and the declared floor is 0.7, so gate on the API's presence rather than on setting `formatexpr` at all.

## Resolution
formatexpr points at a range-aware format.formatexpr(); foldmethod applied via win_findbuf; nvim_buf_set_option replaced with nvim_set_option_value.
title: setup_buffer sets formatexpr to a whole-buffer format and foldmethod on the wrong window

body:
## Problem

`GetShellSpecIndent()` bases every decision on `getline(v:lnum - 1)` — the immediately preceding line, blank or not. A blank line has indent 0, so the fallback at line 45 (`return indent(v:lnum - 1)`) returns 0 for any new line typed after a blank line, wherever it sits in the block structure.

The function is also declared at global scope, so it occupies the name `GetShellSpecIndent` for the whole Vim session rather than being script-local or autoloaded.

## Evidence

`indent/shellspec.vim:10` declares `function! GetShellSpecIndent()`; line 7 wires it with `setlocal indentexpr=GetShellSpecIndent()`.

Failing scenario — pressing `o` on the blank line inside a block:

    Describe "x"
      It "y"
        When call echo hi
                          <- blank line, indent 0
    |                     <- new line lands at column 0, should be column 4

because `prevline` is the blank line, none of the keyword branches match, and `indent(v:lnum - 1)` is 0.

Two further inconsistencies in the same function: line 40 tests `'^\s*Parameters'` without the `\s*$` anchor that line 35 correctly applies to `Data`, and lines 25/30 lack the trailing `\s` that `lua/shellspec/format.lua:55-60` requires — so `Items=3` increments the indent here too.

## Impact

Automatic indentation drops to column 0 after every blank line, which in a spec file means after most logical groupings. The user re-indents by hand, or runs `:ShellSpecFormat` and hits the HEREDOC and range defects filed separately. The global function name can be overwritten by any other plugin defining the same symbol, silently changing this filetype's indentation.

## Fix

Skip blank lines when looking backwards, and scope the function:

    if exists("b:did_indent")
      finish
    endif
    let b:did_indent = 1

    setlocal indentexpr=s:GetShellSpecIndent()
    setlocal indentkeys=!^F,o,O,e,=End

    function! s:GetShellSpecIndent() abort
      let l:prevlnum = prevnonblank(v:lnum - 1)
      if l:prevlnum == 0
        return 0
      endif
      let l:line = getline(v:lnum)
      let l:prevline = getline(l:prevlnum)
      ...
      return indent(l:prevlnum)
    endfunction

Replace every `indent(v:lnum - 1)` with `indent(l:prevlnum)`.

Note that `indentexpr` is evaluated in the script's context, so `s:` works here; if a future change needs it callable from elsewhere, move it to `autoload/shellspec/indent.vim` as `shellspec#indent#get()` rather than returning it to global scope.

While in the file, anchor the keyword patterns to match the Lua implementation (`\s` after block keywords on lines 25 and 30, `\s*$` after `Parameters` on line 40) — see the VimScript block-keyword finding for the same defect in `autoload/shellspec.vim`.

There is no test for `indent/shellspec.vim`; add one that opens a buffer, types past a blank line inside a block, and asserts the resulting indent.

## Resolution
Moved to autoload/shellspec/indent.vim as shellspec#indent#Get() (s: does not resolve in an option expression); prevnonblank used for lookback; patterns anchored.
title: indentexpr ignores blank lines and exposes a global function name

body:
## Problem

`tests/format_spec.lua` has five cases, all calling `M.format_lines` with the default configuration. Nothing exercises the other entry points, the other two formatter implementations, or any non-default setting.

Uncovered, with the defect each gap allowed through this audit:

| Surface | Defect it would have caught |
| --- | --- |
| `autoload/shellspec.vim` (VimScript path) | `<<'EOF'` never detected; unanchored keyword patterns |
| `bin/shellspec-format` stdin mode | `set -e` abort after the first block keyword |
| `M.format_selection` | range re-indented from level 0 |
| `M.format_buffer` | cursor restore against the wrong window |
| `indent/shellspec.vim`, `syntax/shellspec.vim` | blank-line indent reset; unreachable `shellspecTag` |
| `use_spaces = false` (tabs) | `make_indent` ignores `indent_size` in tab mode |
| `indent_comments = false` | never executed |
| `indent_size` other than 2 | never executed |
| `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'` in Lua | pattern branches 2 and 4 of `detect_heredoc_start` never executed |
| Here-strings, unbalanced `End`, empty input | heredoc false positives |

## Evidence

`tests/format_spec.lua:109,133,161,187,213` — five `format.format_lines(...)` calls, no other function under test. `config.setup` at line 85 pins `indent_comments = true`, `indent_size = 2`, `use_spaces = true` for the whole file and is never varied.

Branch coverage of `detect_heredoc_start` (`format.lua:22-29`): only branch 1 (`<<[A-Z_]`) is reached, by test 3. Branches 2, 3 and 4 have no unit test.

`tests/bin_format_spec.sh` is the only coverage of the standalone script, and it fails at its first case today. `tests/integration_test.sh:208-217` is the only mention of the VimScript path, and it asserts only that a command name exists — never what the formatter produces.

## Impact

The suite reports green while three separate implementations disagree about the same input and while documented options have no effect. Every correctness defect in this audit sits in an untested branch; that is not a coincidence but the mechanism.

## Fix

Add to `tests/format_spec.lua`, as plain additions to the existing assert-based harness:

- one case per `detect_heredoc_start` branch: `<<EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`, `<<-EOF`;
- negative cases: `<<<"$x"` here-string, a comment containing `<<EOF`, `<<''`;
- `format_selection` on a nested range, asserting lines outside the range are byte-identical;
- config variations: `use_spaces = false`, `indent_comments = false`, `indent_size = 4`, each re-running `config.setup` and restoring it afterwards;
- edge inputs: empty list, `End` with no opener, a block keyword that also opens a heredoc.

Add a cross-implementation test that runs one fixture through all three formatters and asserts identical output — that single test is what keeps `format.lua`, `autoload/shellspec.vim` and `bin/shellspec-format` from drifting further.

Extend `tests/bin_format_spec.sh` with a stdin-mode case (`printf … | shellspec-format`) asserting the full output line count, and a file-mode case asserting the file mode is preserved.

This is contingent on the suites actually running — fix `((TESTS_PASSED++))` and `run_tests.sh` first, or the new tests are as silent as the old ones.

## Resolution
format_spec.lua grew from 5 to 22 assertions covering every HEREDOC branch, each config option, format_buffer and format_selection; new parity_test.sh covers all three implementations.
title: Test suite covers only format_lines happy paths; two implementations and every non-default option are untested

body:
## Problem

`tests/format_spec.lua` installs a `vim` stub when none exists, so the file can be run as `lua tests/format_spec.lua` — the invocation the README recommends at line 162. The stub's `tbl_deep_extend` is a shallow, last-wins merge:

    tbl_deep_extend = function(behavior, ...)
      local result = {}
      for _, tbl in ipairs({ ... }) do
        if tbl then
          for k, v in pairs(tbl) do result[k] = v end
        end
      end
      return result
    end

Real `vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", …)` recurses into nested tables and merges list-like tables by index. `config.setup` at `config.lua:34` is the only caller, and the difference shows on `heredoc_patterns`, the one nested value in the defaults.

## Evidence

`tests/format_spec.lua:10-20`, quoted above. The stub also omits `vim.log.levels.DEBUG` (lines 24-29 define only `WARN` and `ERROR`) while `format.lua:50,63,78,101,114,120,210` pass `vim.log.levels.DEBUG` to `vim.notify`; the stub's `notify` ignores its second argument, so the `nil` goes unnoticed under the mock and would not under a stricter one.

`vim.g.shellspec_debug = true` at line 35 means the mocked run takes every debug branch in `format.lua`, while the `nvim --headless` run used by `make test-unit` (`Makefile:117`) takes none. The two invocations documented side by side in the README exercise different code paths.

Result: passing under `lua tests/format_spec.lua` is not evidence the code works in Neovim, and vice versa.

## Impact

The standalone path can pass while the plugin is broken in Neovim, and a user-supplied `heredoc_patterns` merges differently in the two environments. The mock is invisible when running under nvim (guarded by `if not vim`), so the divergence never announces itself — the same file simply means different things depending on how it is invoked.

## Fix

Drop the mock and make `nvim --headless` the only supported way to run the unit tests, which is what `Makefile:117` and `tests/run_tests.sh:78` already do:

    if not vim then
      io.stderr:write("tests/format_spec.lua requires Neovim: run `make test-unit`\n")
      os.exit(1)
    end

Then correct README line 162, which currently tells the reader to run `lua tests/format_spec.lua`, and the claim at README line 169 that the suite "includes vim API mocking for standalone execution".

If standalone execution is genuinely wanted, the mock must match real semantics — a recursive `tbl_deep_extend`, the full `vim.log.levels` table — and needs its own test asserting the stub and the real API agree. That is more machinery than one config call justifies; deleting it is the smaller change.

Set `vim.g.shellspec_debug` explicitly in the test file rather than only inside the mock, so both invocations take the same branches.

## Resolution
vim mock removed; the file now requires Neovim and exits with a clear message otherwise. README corrected.
title: The vim mock diverges from real Neovim semantics, so the standalone path tests different behaviour

body:
## Problem

README lines 175-180 state the test architecture rule explicitly:

> The test suite uses **dynamic test generation** to avoid pre-commit hook interference:
> - **No external fixture files**: Test data is defined programmatically within the test scripts
> - **Pre-commit safe**: No `.spec.sh` fixture files that can be modified by formatters

`test_example.spec.sh` is a `.spec.sh` fixture file, committed at the repository root, mode 100755.

## Evidence

`test_example.spec.sh` — 35 lines of deliberately unformatted ShellSpec content (every line at column 0 under nested `Describe`/`Context`/`It` blocks), including a `<<EOF` and a `<<'DATA'` heredoc.

It is referenced only by `.serena/memories/task_completion_checklist.md:34,51,125` as a manual-testing artefact; no automated test opens it.

It matches the plugin's own `*.spec.sh` filetype pattern, so opening it in an editor with `auto_format = true` reformats it — and given the HEREDOC terminator defect filed separately, formatting it produces shell whose heredoc is never closed. The `shfmt` and `shellcheck` pre-commit hooks also claim it (it carries a `#!/bin/bash` shebang), which is precisely the "pre-commit hook interference" the README says the design avoids.

## Impact

The repository's stated convention and its contents disagree, so a contributor reading README:175 has no way to know which is authoritative. The file is a formatter input that the formatter is expected to rewrite, sitting where the tooling will rewrite it — any diff it acquires is noise attributed to whoever last opened it.

## Fix

Pick one and make the repo consistent.

Preferred — delete `test_example.spec.sh` and move its two heredoc cases into `tests/format_spec.lua` as programmatic fixtures, matching the documented architecture. The `<<'DATA'` case in particular is worth keeping: it is the input that exposes the VimScript quoting defect, and no unit test covers it.

Otherwise — keep it as a manual-testing artefact, move it to `examples/` (outside the `*.spec.sh` auto-format and pre-commit scope, or add it to `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as an `exclude:`), and amend README:175-180 to say that one hand-maintained example exists and why.

Update the three `.serena/memories/task_completion_checklist.md` references to whichever path survives.

## Resolution
test_example.spec.sh deleted; its HEREDOC cases moved into format_spec.lua and parity_test.sh. README and .serena notes updated.
title: A committed .spec.sh fixture contradicts the README's own no-fixture-files rule

## Problem

Three linting-configuration problems, all of which weaken or fake coverage:

1. `.mega-linter.yml` is never executed — no workflow runs MegaLinter, and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not reference it. It is 35 lines of configuration for a tool that does not run.
2. Its `ENABLE_LINTERS` allowlist names only `YAML_YAMLLINT`, `MARKDOWN_MARKDOWNLINT`, `YAML_PRETTIER`, `JSON_PRETTIER`, `JAVASCRIPT_ES`, `TYPESCRIPT_ES`. This repository contains no JavaScript or TypeScript, and the list covers none of its Lua, VimScript or shell. Lines 31-32 point both ES linters at `.eslintrc.json`, which does not exist.
3. `.pre-commit-config.yaml:49` runs shellcheck with `args: ["--severity=warning"]`, which discards every `info` and `style` finding.

## Evidence

    $ grep -rn megalinter -i .github/ .pre-commit-config.yaml
    (no matches)
    $ ls .eslintrc.json
    ls: cannot access '.eslintrc.json': No such file or directory

`.mega-linter.yml:21-27` (the allowlist), `:31-32` (the missing config file), `:34-36` (`FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` additionally excluding `.github/workflows`).

The shellcheck narrowing is live, not theoretical — the repo has a real finding hidden by it:

    $ shellcheck bin/shellspec-format tests/*.sh          # default severity
    In bin/shellspec-format line 157:
        printf "%*s" $level "" | tr ' ' '\t'
                     ^----^ SC2086 (info): Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.

With `--severity=warning` that output is empty, so `make lint-shell` reports clean.

`.yamlignore` is tracked and empty (0 lines) — a fourth piece of configuration with no effect.

## Impact

`make lint` reports a clean repository while the only shellcheck finding in it is filtered out, and while 35 lines of linter configuration describe a pipeline that never runs. A reader auditing the repo's quality gates sees MegaLinter, ESLint and shellcheck configured and reasonably concludes the code is covered by all three; none of that is true.

## Fix

Delete `.mega-linter.yml` and `.yamlignore`. The pre-commit config already covers YAML (yamllint), Markdown (markdownlint), shell (shellcheck, shfmt), Lua (stylua) and workflows (actionlint) — MegaLinter adds nothing it is configured to do here.

If MegaLinter is wanted, it needs a workflow, an `ENABLE_LINTERS` list matching the repo's actual languages, and either an `.eslintrc.json` or the removal of lines 26-27 and 31-32.

Drop the severity override so shellcheck runs at its default:

      - repo: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck-precommit
        rev: v0.11.0
        hooks:
          - id: shellcheck

Then fix the one finding it surfaces — `printf "%*s" "$level" ""` at `bin/shellspec-format:157`. Suppress individual checks with `# shellcheck disable=` at the site, or in `.shellcheckrc` as SC2129 already is, rather than by raising the global floor: a per-site suppression records why, a severity floor hides everything of that class forever.

## Resolution
.mega-linter.yml and .yamlignore deleted; shellcheck --severity=warning override removed and the SC2086 it hid is fixed. pre-commit run --all-files passes.

body:
## Problem

Every trim in the script is done by a pipeline of two external processes:

    trimmed=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')

That form appears seven times. On the common path a single input line runs it once in the main loop (line 170), once again inside whichever predicate is consulted (`detect_heredoc_start`, `is_end_keyword`, `is_comment`, `is_block_keyword` — each re-trims the raw line it was handed), plus a command substitution for `$(make_indent …)` at lines 186, 193, 200, 209 and 224.

Bash has had parameter-expansion trimming since 2.02; none of these processes is necessary.

## Evidence

Trim call sites: `bin/shellspec-format:59` (`detect_heredoc_start`), `:84` (`is_heredoc_end`), `:93` (`is_block_keyword`), `:135` (`is_end_keyword`), `:144` (`is_comment`), `:170` (main loop). Indent subshell: `:186,193,200,209,224`.

A non-comment, non-heredoc line reaches `detect_heredoc_start` (2 forks), `is_end_keyword` (2), `is_comment` (2), the main-loop trim (2), `make_indent` (1 subshell) and `is_block_keyword` (2) — 11 processes to reformat one line, none of which does work bash cannot do in-process.

Using `echo` for this is also incorrect for some inputs: a line consisting of `-n`, `-e` or `-E` is consumed as an option by bash's builtin `echo` rather than printed.

## Impact

Formatting is dominated by process creation. A 1000-line spec file spawns on the order of ten thousand processes, turning a millisecond operation into seconds. The `echo` option-eating case additionally corrupts any line whose trimmed form starts with `-n`, `-e` or `-E`.

## Fix

Replace the pipeline with parameter expansion, once, in a helper:

    trim() {
      local s=$1
      s=${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}   # leading
      s=${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}   # trailing
      printf '%s' "$s"
    }

Better still, trim once per line in the main loop and pass `$trimmed` to the predicates instead of `$line`, so each predicate stops re-deriving it — that removes five of the seven call sites outright.

For `make_indent`, drop the command substitution by printing into a variable:

    printf -v indent '%*s' "$((indent_level * INDENT_SIZE))" ''

and reuse `$indent` at lines 186, 193, 200, 209 and 224.

This change touches the same lines as the `set -e` fix; do both in one pass and re-run `tests/bin_format_spec.sh` (which must first be repaired — it currently aborts after its first assertion).

## Resolution
trim() and make_indent() assign to globals via parameter expansion and printf -v; the echo|sed and $(make_indent) forks are gone.
title: The standalone formatter forks three to five subprocesses per input line

## Problem

Symbols that are defined and never reached. Each is small; together they are why several of the defects in this audit stayed invisible — a reader cannot tell which of two copies is live.

- `syntax/shellspec.vim:41` — `syn match shellspecTag … contained` with no container listing it, so it can never match. Its highlight link at line 74 is dead too.
- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:9` — `State.IN_DATA_BLOCK = 3` is never compared against; the state machine has two states.
- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:13` — `get_heredoc_patterns()` is never called.
- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:271` — `M.format_buffer_async` is never called.
- `lua/shellspec/init.lua:49` — `M.health()` duplicates `lua/shellspec/health.lua`'s `M.check()`; `:checkhealth` dispatches to the latter.
- `lua/shellspec/init.lua:82,86` — `M.format_buffer_compat` / `M.format_selection_compat`, commented "Backward compatibility function for VimScript", are unreferenced; the VimScript path uses `autoload/shellspec.vim`.
- `tests/run_tests.sh:54` — the `"command"` branch of `run_test_suite` is never selected; both call sites pass `"script"` or `"nvim_lua"`.

## Evidence

Repository-wide grep for each symbol returns only its definition site (plus, for `heredoc_patterns` and `format_buffer_async`, a README mention filed separately):

    get_heredoc_patterns   format.lua:13                      (definition only)
    format_buffer_async    format.lua:271                     (definition only)
    IN_DATA_BLOCK          format.lua:9                       (definition only)
    format_buffer_compat   init.lua:82                        (definition only)
    format_selection_compat init.lua:86                       (definition only)
    shellspecTag           syntax/shellspec.vim:41,74         (definition + hi link)

`shellspecTag` verified unreachable by inspection: no `syn region` or `syn match` in the file carries `contains=shellspecTag`. The two containers that do list contains are `shellspecString` (`contains=shellspecVariable`, line 44) and `shellspecDataBlock` (`contains=shellspecDataMarker`, line 55).

The duplicate health copy is the concrete cost: `report_start` was removed from Neovim's API and rotted in *both* files, because neither was obviously the live one.

## Impact

ShellSpec tags (`Describe "x" tag:value`) get no highlighting despite a rule existing for them. The rest is dead weight that misleads readers about what is wired — `format_buffer_async` in particular backs a README feature claim, and `M.health` is a second, equally broken implementation of a check that already exists.

## Fix

Delete `State.IN_DATA_BLOCK`, `get_heredoc_patterns` (or wire it up per the config finding), `M.format_buffer_compat`, `M.format_selection_compat`, `M.health` from `init.lua:49-79`, and the `"command"` branch of `run_test_suite`.

For `shellspecTag`, either wire it into the block-keyword lines that can carry tags, or drop the rule and its `hi def link`:

    syn match shellspecBlockLine "^\s*\(x\|f\)\?\(Describe\|Context\|ExampleGroup\|It\|Specify\|Example\)\>.*$"
          \ contains=shellspecBlock,shellspecString,shellspecTag

For `format_buffer_async`, decide with the README:42 claim — wire it to a command or remove both.

## Resolution
Removed IN_DATA_BLOCK, format_buffer_compat, format_selection_compat, init.lua M.health and run_test_suite's command branch; get_heredoc_patterns and format_buffer_async wired up; shellspecTag given a container.

body:
## Problem

- `autoload/shellspec.vim:8` — `silent! %delete _` discards the error when the buffer is `nomodifiable` or read-only. `setline(1, l:formatted)` on the next line then also fails, and its return value is ignored, so `:ShellSpecFormat` reports success while the buffer is unchanged.
- `lua/shellspec/health.lua:32,41,49` — `health.report_error("Failed to load …: " .. config)` concatenates the `pcall` error directly. A `pcall` error may be a table (any `error({…})` in a loaded module), and concatenating one raises inside the health check.
- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:248` — `pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, 0, cursor_pos)` silently drops the failure. The cursor restore fails whenever formatting shortened the buffer past the saved row, which is exactly when the user most needs to know the cursor moved.
- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:242,248` — the cursor is read and written against window `0` while the lines are written to `bufnr`; when `bufnr` is not the current window's buffer, the plugin saves and restores an unrelated window's cursor.

## Evidence

`autoload/shellspec.vim:8-10`:

    silent! %delete _
    call setline(1, l:formatted)
    call setpos('.', l:pos)

No return value is checked and no error can escape.

`lua/shellspec/health.lua:32` — `health.report_error("Failed to load ShellSpec configuration: " .. config)`, where `config` is the second `pcall` return. Same shape at lines 41 and 49.

`lua/shellspec/format.lua:242` reads the cursor from window `0`; line 245 writes lines to `bufnr`; line 248 restores into window `0`.

The health-check concatenation is currently unreachable only because the three `require`s in question do not raise table errors — it is one `error({code = …})` in a dependency away from turning a diagnostic into a crash.

## Impact

A user who runs `:ShellSpecFormat` in a read-only buffer on Vim sees no output and no error, and reasonably concludes the file was already formatted. The health check, whose whole job is to report failure legibly, can itself fail with a type error while reporting one.

## Fix

In `autoload/shellspec.vim#format_buffer`, check modifiability up front and drop the `silent!`:

    if !&modifiable
      echohl ErrorMsg | echomsg 'ShellSpec: buffer is not modifiable' | echohl NONE
      return
    endif
    %delete _
    call setline(1, l:formatted)
    call setpos('.', l:pos)

In `lua/shellspec/health.lua`, coerce the error: `.. tostring(config)` at lines 32, 41 and 49 (this file is being rewritten anyway for the `report_*` API removal — do both together).

In `lua/shellspec/format.lua`, resolve the window from the buffer rather than assuming the current one, and clamp the restored position:

    local win = vim.fn.bufwinid(bufnr == 0 and vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() or bufnr)
    if win ~= -1 then
      local pos = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(win)
      ...
      pos[1] = math.min(pos[1], vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(bufnr))
      vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(win, pos)
    end

With the position clamped, the `pcall` is no longer papering over a foreseeable failure and can be dropped.

## Resolution
autoload checks &modifiable and drops silent!; health.lua uses tostring on pcall errors; format_buffer resolves the window via bufwinid and clamps the cursor instead of pcall-swallowing.
title: Four error paths that swallow or mishandle failures

body:
## Problem

Every `mktemp` in the repository is cleaned up only on the success path. No script installs a `trap`, so `Ctrl-C` or `SIGTERM` between creation and removal leaves the file behind.

Separately, `tests/integration_test.sh:210` runs `vim` with no `timeout` and no stdin redirect, unlike the seven `nvim` invocations above it which all use `timeout 10 … </dev/null`. If that `vim` waits for input it blocks forever.

## Evidence

Unguarded temp files: `bin/shellspec-format:291` (removed only at line 296 on the failure branch, or consumed by `mv` at 293); `tests/integration_test.sh:96,107-108,152-153` (removed at 103, 148, 197); `tests/golden_master_test.sh:195-197` (removed at 234).

`tests/integration_test.sh:210`:

    if vim -u NONE -c "set rtp+=$PROJECT_ROOT" -c "source plugin/shellspec.vim" -c "if exists(':ShellSpecFormat') | echo 'SUCCESS' | endif" -c "quit" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "SUCCESS"; then

compared with line 201 for the nvim equivalent:

    if timeout 10 nvim --headless -u NONE … </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -q "ShellSpec.nvim"; then

`tests/run_tests.sh:84` wraps the whole suite in `timeout 30`, which bounds the hang but reports it as the fabricated "known issue with test environment nvim interaction" rather than as a hung test.

The leak is what `Makefile:243` was reaching for with its system-wide `find /tmp -name "*shellspec*" -delete` — a far more dangerous cure than the disease.

## Impact

Interrupted formatter runs and interrupted test runs accumulate files in `/tmp`. The unbounded `vim` invocation makes the integration suite's runtime depend on whether a terminal is attached, which is part of why the suite was written off as environmentally flaky.

## Fix

Add a trap next to each `mktemp`. In `bin/shellspec-format`, inside the per-file loop:

    temp_file=$(mktemp "${file}.shellspec-format.XXXXXX")
    trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' EXIT INT TERM

(the same line the file-mode-preservation fix needs — apply both together).

In the test scripts, register cleanup once per suite:

    TMPFILES=()
    cleanup() { rm -f "${TMPFILES[@]}"; }
    trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

and append each `mktemp` result to `TMPFILES` instead of removing it inline.

Give the `vim` invocation the same guards as its nvim siblings:

    if timeout 10 vim -u NONE -e -s -c "set rtp+=$PROJECT_ROOT" … </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -q "SUCCESS"; then

`-e -s` puts vim in silent Ex mode, which is the vim equivalent of `--headless` and removes the reason it would wait for a terminal.

## Resolution
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM plus a TMPFILES registry in all four shell suites and in bin/shellspec-format; the vim invocation gained -N -e -s, timeout and </dev/null.
title: mktemp without trap leaks temp files on interrupt, and one test can hang unbounded

body:
## Problem

Three documentation gaps on the plugin's public surface:

1. There is no `doc/` directory, so `:help shellspec` finds nothing. A Vim plugin's help file is how its commands, options and global variables are discoverable from inside the editor; the README is not reachable there.
2. Every public Lua function carries a one-line comment restating its name — `-- Setup function`, `-- Get configuration value`, `-- Format entire buffer`, `-- Format selection`, `-- Cleanup function`. None records what a reader cannot recover from the body: which buffer `format_selection`'s `start_line` is 1-indexed against, that `format_buffer` swallows its own errors via `pcall` and notifies instead of raising, that `config.setup` silently accepts unknown keys, or that `M.cleanup` clears the whole augroup including registrations made by other callers.
3. The Vim/legacy configuration section (README:102-114) documents `g:shellspec_auto_format` and `g:shellspec_indent_comments` but no indent-size variable — because `autoload/shellspec.vim:68,76,84,94,116` hardcodes `repeat('  ', …)`. The Lua path's `indent_size` and `use_spaces` have no VimScript equivalent, and the README does not say so.

## Evidence

    $ ls doc/
    ls: cannot access 'doc/': No such file or directory

Comments that restate the signature: `config.lua:32` (`-- Setup function`), `config.lua:43` (`-- Get configuration value`), `format.lua:233` (`-- Format entire buffer`), `format.lua:260` (`-- Format selection`), `autocmds.lua:105` (`-- Cleanup function`), `init.lua:12` (`-- Setup function for Lua configuration`).

Hardcoded VimScript indent: `autoload/shellspec.vim:68,76,84,94,116` — `repeat('  ', l:indent)`, five sites, no configuration path. README:78 documents `indent_size = 2` under the Lua section only, with no note that the fallback ignores it.

## Impact

A user on Vim who sets a 4-space indent convention gets 2 spaces with no error and no documented reason. `:help shellspec` — the first thing a Vim user tries — returns nothing. And a contributor reading `format_selection` has no way to learn from the code that its `bufnr` and the window whose cursor it manipulates can differ, which is one of the defects filed in this audit.

## Fix

Add `doc/shellspec.txt` with the standard tag structure — `*shellspec.txt*`, `*shellspec-commands*`, `*shellspec-configuration*`, `*shellspec-vim*` — covering both commands, both configuration surfaces, and the filetype patterns that actually work. Add `doc/tags` to `.gitignore`; Vim generates it with `:helptags`.

Replace the restating comments with docstrings that record the constraint rather than the name, per this repo's own documentation convention. For example, on `format_selection`:

    --- Reformats buffer lines [start_line, end_line], 1-indexed against `bufnr`.
    --- Indentation is derived from the first line's existing indent, not from the
    --- enclosing block: a selection whose opening keyword lies outside the range
    --- is re-indented relative to itself.

For the VimScript indent width, either read `&shiftwidth` in `shellspec#format_lines` — `let l:sw = repeat(' ', &shiftwidth)` — or state plainly in README:102-114 that the fallback always emits two spaces and that `indent_size`/`use_spaces` are Neovim-only.

## Resolution
Added doc/shellspec.txt; public Lua functions documented with why-not-what docstrings; VimScript path now honours shiftwidth/expandtab and README says so.
title: No Vim help file, and the public Lua surface carries no docstrings

## Problem

- `.gitignore` is 134 lines of PHP and Node boilerplate — `composer.phar`, `/vendor/`, `.phpunit.result.cache`, `.php-cs-fixer.cache`, `node_modules/`, `jspm_packages/`, `bower_components`, `.rts2_cache_umd/`.     $ ls composer.json package.json Gemfile pyproject.toml 2>&1 | head -1
    ls: cannot access 'composer.json': No such file or directory
    $ ls .github/labels.yml
    ls: cannot access '.github/labels.yml': No such file or directory

Replace `.gitignore` with the handful of entries this project generates:

    *.bak
    *.tmp
    doc/tags
    .DS_Store

Either add `.github/labels.yml` (if the shared `ivuorinen/actions/sync-labels` action is meant to read a local definition) or drop lines 10-12 from `sync-labels.yml` so the workflow's triggers match what exists.

Change `Makefile:165` to a plain comment so the awk filter skips it:

    # Internal release target (use release-* targets instead)
    _release:
