body:
## Problem

The same state machine — trim, detect HEREDOC start, detect `End`, detect comment, detect block keyword, emit with indent — exists three times:

- `lua/shellspec/format.lua:18-231` (Lua, Neovim 0.7+)
- `autoload/shellspec.vim:14-126` (VimScript fallback)
- `bin/shellspec-format:56-233` (bash, standalone CLI)

Each maintains its own copy of the keyword list, the HEREDOC pattern list and the indent logic. Nothing tests them against each other, and they have drifted on every axis.

## Evidence

Divergences found, all confirmed by execution:

| Behaviour | format.lua | autoload | bin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Block keyword needs trailing space | yes (`^Describe%s`) | **no** (`^\(Describe\|…\)`) | yes (`[[:space:]]`) |
| Standalone hook needs end-of-line | yes (`%s*$`) | **no** | yes (`[[:space:]]*$`) |
| `<<'EOF'` detected | yes | **no** (quoting defect, line 20) | yes |
| Indent width configurable | `indent_size` | **hardcoded 2 spaces** | `--indent-size` |
| Tabs supported | `use_spaces` | **no** | `--tabs` |
| Comment indent toggle | `indent_comments` | `g:shellspec_indent_comments` | `--no-comment-indent` |

So `Items=3` opens a block in the VimScript path and not in the other two; `<<'DATA'` preserves its body in two of three; a 4-space indent is honoured by two of three. The defects filed separately against `autoload/shellspec.vim` are all of this shape — a fix applied to one copy and not the others.

Test coverage reinforces the split: `tests/format_spec.lua` tests only the Lua copy, `tests/bin_format_spec.sh` only the bash copy, and the VimScript copy has none.

## Impact

The same spec file formats three different ways depending on whether it is opened in Neovim, in Vim, or piped through the CLI — which defeats the purpose of a formatter. Every future fix must be made three times in three languages, and nothing detects when it is not.

## Fix

Short term, add the test that makes drift visible: one fixture set, run through all three implementations, asserting byte-identical output. This does not remove the duplication but converts a silent divergence into a failing test, and it is cheap — the golden-master harness at `tests/golden_master_test.sh:180-235` already shells out to nvim and diffs, so it needs a second and third invocation per case rather than new machinery.

Medium term, reduce three copies to two. `bin/shellspec-format` is genuinely separate (it must run without an editor), but the VimScript fallback exists only for Vim and pre-0.7 Neovim. Given `plugin/shellspec.vim:15` already gates on `has('nvim-0.7')` and 0.7 shipped in 2022, consider whether the VimScript copy still earns its keep; deleting it removes the least-tested and most-divergent of the three, and the README's "Backward compatibility" bullet (line 43) then needs to state the real floor.

If it stays, at minimum bring it to parity: the anchoring fix, the `<<'EOF'` quoting fix, and `&shiftwidth`-derived indent width are each filed separately and together close the table above.

This finding is the arch lens applied inline; `docs/audit/arch-profile.md` was not generated.

## Resolution
tests/parity_test.sh runs one fixture through all three implementations and requires byte-identical output; all divergences in the finding's table closed.
title: One formatting algorithm maintained as three hand-synchronised copies that have drifted apart

body:
## Problem

Finding `audit-89efae00` claimed three of the four documented filetype patterns "never fire", on the strength of a measurement that opened every file by absolute path. That was the wrong measurement.

Vim matches an autocmd pattern containing a slash against **both** the buffer name as typed and the full path. `nvim spec/foo.sh` — the ordinary way anyone opens a file — matches `spec/*.sh` on the as-typed name. `*` also spans `/` in autocmd patterns, so the same rule already covered arbitrary nesting below `spec/`.

So the real defect was much narrower than filed: the patterns worked for relative opens and failed only for absolute ones. Acting on the wrong premise, the fix replaced `spec/*.sh` with `*/spec/*.sh` and **deleted `test/*.sh` entirely**, removing working, documented behaviour.

## Evidence

Measured against the committed `ftdetect/shellspec.vim`, same files, two invocation forms:

    opened by RELATIVE path (what the audit never tried)
      spec/plain.sh       -> shellspec
      test/plain.sh       -> shellspec
      spec/unit/deep.sh   -> shellspec

    opened by ABSOLUTE path (all the audit tried)
      /abs/.../spec/plain.sh -> ''
      /abs/.../test/plain.sh -> ''

Both directory rules worked; only the absolute-path form did not.

After restoring `test/` coverage and registering each directory rule in both forms, all eight cases resolve to `shellspec`:

    relative: spec/plain.sh, spec/unit/deep.sh, test/plain.sh, test/unit/deep.sh, x_spec.sh
    absolute: spec/plain.sh, spec/unit/deep.sh, test/plain.sh, test/unit/deep.sh

`audit-89efae00`'s narrow claim — that absolute-path opens failed — was correct, and the `*/` prefix fixes it. Its headline claim and the `test/*.sh` removal were not.

## Impact

Had the change shipped, every project keeping specs in `test/` would have silently lost syntax highlighting, indentation, commands and formatting — a documented feature removed on a false premise, and removed from users who were using it.

The `test/*.sh` rule is genuinely broad: it claims every shell script under any `test/` directory, not only specs. That is worth a decision, but it is the maintainer's decision about working behaviour, not something an audit should have quietly deleted.

## Fix

Already applied. Each directory rule is now registered in both forms, in `ftdetect/shellspec.vim` and in the Lua `BufRead,BufNewFile` autocmd:

    spec/*.sh    */spec/*.sh
    test/*.sh    */test/*.sh

README and `doc/shellspec.txt` now state that `test/` is covered, explain the as-typed-vs-full-path duplication, and note the breadth of `test/*.sh` with an override for anyone who wants it narrower:

    autocmd BufRead,BufNewFile test/*.sh setfiletype sh

Open question for the maintainer, deliberately not decided here: should `test/*.sh` be narrowed to `test/*_spec.sh`? It would stop hijacking ordinary shell scripts, at the cost of dropping specs in `test/` that are not named `*_spec.sh`. Current behaviour is preserved until that is decided.

Method note: when a pattern's behaviour depends on how a buffer is opened, measure every invocation form before concluding it is dead. One form disproving a pattern is not the pattern being dead.

## Resolution
Correction applied and decided. Each spec/ rule registered in both as-typed and */ forms, so relative and absolute opens both work. test/*.sh narrowed per maintainer decision: the directory rule is removed entirely, because *_spec.sh and *.spec.sh are basename-matched and already cover spec files under test/ at any depth -- test/*_spec.sh would have been pure redundancy. Ordinary .sh under test/ is no longer claimed; documented as a breaking change in README and doc/shellspec.txt with a one-line restore. Integration test 4b pins all four boundaries by BOTH relative and absolute path.
title: CORRECTION: spec/*.sh and test/*.sh did fire — audit-89efae00 tested only absolute paths

## Problem

Finding `audit-a5b14dd8` claimed `.mega-linter.yml` was orphaned because "no workflow runs MegaLinter, and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not reference it". That conclusion was reached by grepping this repository only. It is wrong.

`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml` calls `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint`, a composite action whose implementation lives in another repository. That action runs MegaLinter. `.mega-linter.yml` is therefore read on every push and pull request to `main`.

The file was deleted on the strength of that wrong claim and has been restored byte-identical to its committed version. The `.yamlignore` deletion, bundled into the same finding on the same reasoning, has also been reverted.

The remaining `.mega-linter.yml` criticisms in `audit-a5b14dd8` do not hold up either. The `ENABLE_LINTERS` allowlist covers YAML, Markdown and JSON while `.pre-commit-config.yaml` covers Lua, shell, VimScript and workflows — that is a coherent division of labour between the two tools, not a coverage gap.

Only the shellcheck half of `audit-a5b14dd8` was valid: `--severity=warning` did hide a real SC2086, demonstrated by running shellcheck at default severity. That part remains correctly fixed.

## Evidence

`ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint/action.yml` at the pinned SHA `6a8c40d9c5ff01b901d382b0ef86d432215aae2a`:

    name: PR Lint
    description: Runs MegaLinter against pull requests
    ...
    - name: MegaLinter
      uses: oxsecurity/megalinter/flavors/cupcake@9949bad031045f366be2467e00e8371a7328a2e2 # v10.1.0
      id: ml
      env:
        ...
        # ADD YOUR CUSTOM ENV VARIABLES HERE OR DEFINE THEM IN A FILE
        # .mega-linter.yml AT THE ROOT OF YOUR REPOSITORY

The action names the config file explicitly.

Two settings in `.mega-linter.yml` are nonetheless inert, because MegaLinter resolves environment variables ahead of the config file — megalinter.io/latest/config-file: "When configuration variables are defined in both environment variables and the .mega-linter.yml file, the environment variable takes precedence."

    OVERRIDDEN  VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: repo says 'true' -> action env forces 'false'
    OVERRIDDEN  APPLY_FIXES:           repo says 'all'  -> action env forces 'none'

Everything else in the file has no counterpart in the action's env block and is honoured: the reporters, `ENABLE_LINTERS`, `DISABLE_LINTERS`, the `*_CONFIG_FILE` pointers and `FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE`.

`JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE` and `TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE` both point at `.eslintrc.json`, which does not exist. This is inert today — `git ls-files '*.js' '*.ts' '*.jsx' '*.tsx'` returns 0 files, so the two ES linters have nothing to run on.

## Impact

The audit deleted a load-bearing CI config file. Had that reached `main`, MegaLinter would have fallen back to cupcake-flavor defaults on every PR: the `ENABLE_LINTERS` allowlist gone, `DISABLE_LINTERS: REPOSITORY_DEVSKIM` gone, the yamllint and markdownlint config pointers gone, and `FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` gone — a much broader and noisier lint run against different rules.

The two overridden settings are a smaller, live issue: the repository's config states it validates the whole codebase and applies fixes, and it does neither. Anyone reading `.mega-linter.yml` to learn what CI does is misled on both counts.

## Fix

No change to `.mega-linter.yml` is required for it to work; it is already correct and restored.

For the two inert settings, decide which side owns them and make the file say what actually happens. Either drop the two lines, since the action decides:

    # VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE and APPLY_FIXES are set by ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint
    # and cannot be overridden here -- MegaLinter resolves env vars ahead of
    # this file. Change them in the action, not here.

or, if full-codebase validation is genuinely wanted for this repo, set `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: true` as a workflow-level `env:` in `.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml`, which does take precedence.

For the ES linter config: either add a minimal `.eslintrc.json`, or drop `JAVASCRIPT_ES`, `TYPESCRIPT_ES` and their two `*_CONFIG_FILE` lines until the repository actually contains JavaScript. Leaving them is harmless now but breaks the first PR that adds a `.js` file.

Method note for future runs: a workflow step that calls a third-party or org-level composite action is not evidence that nothing consumes a config file. Resolve the action and read it — `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>/action.yml?ref=<pinned-sha>` — before concluding any config is orphaned.

## Resolution
File restored (it is live via ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint) and its two inert settings removed: VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE and APPLY_FIXES are forced by the action's env block, which MegaLinter resolves ahead of the config file, so a header comment now records where they are controlled instead of stating a value that does nothing. JAVASCRIPT_ES/TYPESCRIPT_ES and both .eslintrc.json pointers dropped (repo has 0 JS/TS files); the now-redundant DISABLE_LINTERS also dropped, since ENABLE_LINTERS is already an allowlist. FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE trimmed to paths that exist plus docs/audit. yamllint clean.
title: CORRECTION: .mega-linter.yml is live, not orphaned — audit-a5b14dd8 was wrong

## Problem

Re-checking every deletion the audit made against consumers *outside* this repository turned up three more instances of the same reasoning error, beyond the MegaLinter one already recorded in `audit-502b02ad`.

**1. Public Lua API removed from a tagged release.** `audit-30b0a174` listed `M.health`, `M.format_buffer_compat` and `M.format_selection_compat` as "declared-but-unreachable" and they were deleted. They are exported from `require("shellspec")` in a plugin tagged `v2.0.2`. A repo-local grep cannot see the callers, because the callers are users' Neovim configs. Removing them is a semver-major change made in a cleanup pass.

**2. A live config regression introduced by wiring up `heredoc_patterns`.** `audit-f82e7547` correctly found the option was never read, and the fix made `detect_heredoc_start` read it. But the pattern values this project's own README published carry no capture group. Once read, `string.match` returns the whole match, so the "delimiter" becomes `<<EOF` rather than `EOF` — which no terminator line can equal, leaving the formatter stuck in HEREDOC state to end of file. Anyone who had copied the README config block verbatim would have had their formatting silently halt.

**3. A path filter deleted on a wrong assumption about a shared action.** `audit-8535af99` called the `.github/labels.yml` entry in `sync-labels.yml` dead because the file does not exist here. `ivuorinen/actions/sync-labels` documents that input as defaulting to `.github/labels.yml` relative to the repository root, with a missing manifest being "a warning + successful no-op, not an error". The filter was forward-looking and correct.

## Evidence

**1.** Public surface diff against HEAD, and the tag:

    removed: M.format_buffer_compat, M.format_selection_compat, M.health
    kept:    M.config, M.format_buffer, M.format_lines, M.format_selection, M.setup, M._VERSION
    $ git tag --list 'v*' | tail -1
    v2.0.2

**2.** The old README's `heredoc_patterns` block, fed to the wired-up code:

    [Describe "x"]
    [  It "y"]
    [    When call cat <<EOF]
    [body]
    [EOF]
    [The output should equal "body"]   <- unformatted
    [End]                              <- unformatted
    [End]

The last three lines never get formatted: the formatter is waiting for a line equal to `<<EOF`.

**3.** `ivuorinen/actions/sync-labels/action.yml` at the pinned SHA:

    inputs:
      labels:
        description: "Path to the labels manifest (YAML or JSON), relative to the
          repository root. Defaults to .github/labels.yml when omitted ...
          A missing manifest is a warning + successful no-op, not an error."

## Impact

Each would have shipped a regression to fix a cosmetic complaint: a breaking API change without a version bump, a formatter that silently stops on a documented configuration, and a workflow that would no longer react to the labels manifest being added.

The common cause is treating "grep finds no caller in this repository" as proof a symbol or setting is unused. For a published plugin's exported functions, for config values consumed by third-party actions, and for values a user supplies, the callers are by definition outside the tree being grepped.

## Fix

All three reverted or guarded, with regression tests.

**1.** The three functions are restored in `lua/shellspec/init.lua` as documented deprecated aliases delegating to the live implementations — `M.health` now calls `shellspec.health.check`, so it works rather than raising on the removed `vim.health.report_*` API. Removal can happen at the next major bump. Test 14c asserts all three stay exported.

**2.** `config.validate_heredoc_patterns` drops any pattern with no capture group, naming it and showing a correct example, and falls back to the defaults when none survives. This restores the pre-change behaviour for a legacy config instead of breaking it, and says why. Test 14b covers the exact legacy block.

**3.** The `.github/labels.yml` path filter is restored; `sync-labels.yml` now differs from HEAD only by the pre-existing dependency-bump SHA.

The remaining live question there is unchanged and untouched: `.github/labels.yml` does not exist, so the daily label sync is a no-op. Adding a manifest, or dropping the workflow, is the maintainer's call.

## Resolution
All three reverted or guarded, and the remaining live item closed: .github/labels.yml now exists, so the daily label sync is no longer a no-op. Manifest is scoped to this project and derived from actual usage across 140 closed PRs and 1 issue; verified that all 7 in-use labels survive the action's default prune: true, and that every label renovate, the stale action and the issue templates depend on is present. bug_report.md's 'labels: bug' corrected to 'bugfix' -- 'bug' was never defined on the repo.
title: CORRECTION: three more "unused" conclusions drawn from repo-local greps alone

## Problem

`format_shellspec` reads input with `while IFS= read -r line; do` (bin/shellspec-format:183). `read` returns non-zero on a final line that lacks a terminating newline, so the loop exits without processing it and the line is never printed. In file mode the truncated output is then `mv`'d over the original.

## Evidence

Reproduced:

```
printf 'Describe "x"\nIt "y"\nEnd\nEnd' > p4_file_spec.sh
bin/shellspec-format p4_file_spec.sh
cat -A p4_file_spec.sh
Describe "x"$
  It "y"$
  End$
```

The last `End` is gone, exit status 0. Stdin mode drops it the same way. The Lua path keeps the line (`format_lines` works on a list).

## Impact

Silent loss of user content on in-place formatting of any file saved without a final newline (common from editors with `nofixeol`, generators, Windows tools). The dropped `End` also leaves the spec structurally broken.

## Fix

Change the loop header to `while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do`. Add a bin_format_spec.sh regression that pipes `printf 'Describe "x"\nEnd'` (no trailing newline) and asserts both lines are present, in stdin and in-place mode.

## Resolution
Loop is now `while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]`; bin_format_spec.sh asserts an unterminated last line survives stdin and in-place modes.
title: bin/shellspec-format silently deletes a final line that has no trailing newline

body:
## Problem

`if format_shellspec <"$file" >"$temp_file"; then ... mv "$temp_file" "$file"` (bin/shellspec-format:309-314). A function called as an `if` condition runs with `set -e` suppressed, and its status is that of the `while` loop's last body command, which is 0 regardless of earlier `printf` failures. The `else` branch ("Failed to format") is effectively unreachable, and a failed write (ENOSPC, quota, EIO) still reaches the `mv`.

## Evidence

A copy of the script with only the temp redirect pointed at `/dev/full`:

```
fmt_devfull p5_spec.sh; echo exit=$?; wc -c < p5_spec.sh
... printf: write error: No space left on device   (x4)
exit=0
0
```

The original 4-line spec is replaced by a 0-byte file, and the script exits 0. Stdin mode exits 1 on the same failure, because there `set -e` is active.

## Impact

On a full disk or over quota, formatting a spec in place destroys it and reports success, so a pre-commit hook or CI step carries on.

## Fix

Make the function report write failure explicitly. Inside `format_shellspec`, replace each `printf ... ` with `printf ... || return 1` (or wrap the loop body so any failed printf returns 1). Then keep the existing `if/else`, which will now take the error branch. Add a regression that makes the temp path unwritable (for example `chmod a-w` on a directory holding the target) and asserts the original is unchanged and the exit is non-zero.

## Resolution
Every printf in format_shellspec ends in `|| return 1`, so the existing else branch now runs on write failure; regression uses `ulimit -f 0` with SIGXFSZ ignored and asserts non-zero exit and an intact file.
title: In-place mode ignores write failures and replaces the file with truncated output

body:
## Problem

Every implementation requires the delimiter to follow `<<`/`<<-` immediately and to be uppercase:

- config.lua:17 `"<<%-?([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)"`
- autoload/shellspec.vim:27 `'<<-\?\([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\)'`
- bin/shellspec-format:95 `"<<-?([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)"`

POSIX allows blanks between `<<` and the word (`cat << EOF`, the most common spelling), lowercase words (`<<eof`) and backslash quoting (`<<\EOF`). None of these match, so the body and terminator are re-indented as ordinary lines — the exact failure the prior audit-431dc480 fix was meant to prevent.

## Evidence

Input `When call cat << EOF` / `body` / `EOF` inside an `It`. All three implementations produce:

```
    When call cat << EOF$
    body$
    EOF$
```

Running bash on the result: `warning: here-document at line 1 delimited by end-of-file (wanted 'EOF')`, and the indented `    EOF` plus everything after it becomes heredoc body.

## Impact

Formatting a valid spec produces shell that no longer parses as intended: the heredoc swallows the rest of the file. It also corrupts heredoc bodies whose indentation is significant.

## Fix

Allow optional blanks, backslash and lowercase in all three copies:

- Lua: `"<<%-?%s*\\?([%a_][%w_]*)"`, `"<<%-?%s*'([^']+)'"`, `'<<%-?%s*"([^"]+)"'`
- VimScript: `'<<-\?\s*\\\?\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\)'` and the quoted forms with `\s*`
- bash: `"<<-?[[:space:]]*\\\\?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)"` and the quoted forms with `[[:space:]]*`

Update the README/doc defaults, and add `<< EOF`, `<<eof` and `<<\EOF` cases to the parity fixture and format_spec.lua.

## Resolution
All three implementations accept blanks after <<, lowercase words and a backslash; lines containing (( are never HEREDOC openers (arithmetic shift). Covered in parity fixture, format_spec.lua Test 18 and bin_format_spec.sh; README/doc updated.
title: `<< EOF` (space), lowercase and backslash-quoted heredocs are not detected, so their terminator is indented

body:
## Problem

The block grammar (format.lua:17-36, autoload/shellspec.vim:15-20, bin/shellspec-format:128-155, indent.vim:12-16) only knows Describe/Context/ExampleGroup/It/Specify/Example, bare `Data`/`Parameters` and hooks. ShellSpec's `Mock <name>`, `Data:raw`, `Data:expand` and `Parameters:block|value|matrix|dynamic` also open blocks closed by `End`. The installed shellspec 0.28.1 `lib/` contains all of them as line-start keywords. Their body is not indented, and their `End` pops the *enclosing* level, so everything after it shifts left.

## Evidence

Input (flat) → Lua output; VimScript and bin are byte-identical:

```
Describe "x"
  Mock date
  echo 2019
End            <- closes Describe, not Mock
It "y"
  Data:raw
  #|a
End
When call f
End
Parameters:block
...
```

The syntax file already highlights `Data:expand` and `Parameters:value|matrix|dynamic` (syntax/shellspec.vim:36-37), so the formatter and the syntax disagree about the grammar.

## Impact

Any spec that uses mocks, raw/expand data or parameterised examples is mis-indented from that point to the end of the file on every format, including format-on-save.

## Fix

Add `^Mock%s`, `^Data:%a+%s*$` and `^Parameters:%a+%s*$` to BLOCK_PATTERNS. Add the equivalents `'^Mock\s'`, `'^\(Data\|Parameters\):\a\+\s*$'` to autoload/shellspec.vim and the indent.vim `s:block_pattern`, and `^(Mock[[:space:]]|(Data|Parameters):[a-z]+[[:space:]]*$)` to `is_block_keyword` in bin. Add a Mock/Data:raw/Parameters:block case to the parity fixture.

## Resolution
Mock, Data:<mod> and Parameters:<mod> added to format.lua, autoload/shellspec.vim, bin and indent.vim; covered by parity fixture, golden case blocks_and_pipes, unit Test 19 and the integration gg=G check.
title: Mock, Data:raw/:expand and Parameters:block/:value/:matrix/:dynamic blocks are not recognised as blocks

## Problem

`format_selection` seeds the level with `indent_level_of(lines[1])` (format.lua:227, autoload/shellspec.vim:173). An `End` line sits at the level of its opener, but `format_lines` decrements *before* emitting `End`. So a range whose first line is `End` starts one level too deep and then drops a level, and every following line shifts left by one level. `formatexpr` (format.lua:242) routes `gq` through the same path.

## Evidence

On an already-correct 8-line spec, with folds disabled so the range is not widened:

- `:4,8ShellSpecFormatRange` → lines 4-7 become `End`, `It "z"`, `  When call g`, `End` (each one level too shallow).
- `gqq` on line 4 (`  End`) → `End`.
- `gqG` from line 4 → same as the range command.
- Visual `4GVj:ShellSpecFormatRange` → `End` / `It "z"` flattened.

Direct `format_lines({'  End','  It "z"',...}, 1)` returns `{'End','It "z"','  When call g','End','End'}`.

## Impact

Running the formatter on a correctly formatted region breaks it. `gq` motions and visual reformat commonly begin at an `End` line.

## Fix

In both implementations, when the first line is an `End` keyword, seed with `indent_level_of(lines[1]) + 1`: Lua `local seed = indent_level_of(lines[1]); if is_end_keyword(vim.trim(lines[1])) then seed = seed + 1 end`; VimScript the same check on `trim(l:lines[0]) =~# '^End\s*$'`. Add unit tests for a range and for `formatexpr` starting on `End`, asserting an already-formatted buffer is unchanged.

## Resolution
format_selection (Lua and VimScript) seeds one level deeper when the first line is End; unit Test 17 asserts ranges 4-8 and 4-4 are idempotent on formatted code.
title: Range formatting and gq starting on an End line corrupt correctly formatted code

## Problem

plugin/shellspec.vim:15 selects the Lua implementation for `has('nvim-0.7')`, doc/shellspec.txt:24 and README declare 0.7, and the new CI matrix tests `v0.7.2` (test.yml:33). Two APIs the Lua path uses do not exist that early:

- `vim.health.start/ok/info/warn/error` (health.lua:12+) — first defined in v0.10.0. Before that, 0.8/0.9 have only `report_*`, and 0.7 has no `vim.health` module at all.

Upstream sources via `gh api repos/neovim/neovim/contents/...`:

- `runtime/lua/vim/health.lua`: ABSENT at v0.7.2; only `function M.report_start` at v0.8.0 and v0.9.0; `function M.start` and `function M.ok` first appear at v0.10.0.

On 0.7 every shellspec FileType event errors from `setup_buffer`. On 0.7-0.9 `:checkhealth shellspec` crashes — the failure the prior audit-89ee7df9 fix claimed to remove, now moved to the other end of the supported range. The new CI `v0.7.2` job will fail on first run.

body:
## Problem

ftdetect/shellspec.vim:13-16 uses `setfiletype shellspec`. `setfiletype` is a no-op once a filetype is set, and the runtime's own `*.sh` rule fires first and sets `sh`. Vim has no other detection path — the Lua autocmd exists only on Neovim — so the Vim fallback never gets a shellspec buffer. Its FileType settings, syntax, indent and format-on-save never activate.

## Evidence

A normal install (plugin on 'runtimepath' before `filetype on`), then `:edit ft_spec.sh`:

- Vim → `&ft` = `sh`
- Neovim with only ftdetect active → `sh`
- Neovim `--clean` with the full plugin → `shellspec`, only because autocmds.lua forces `filetype=`.

## Impact

The whole VimScript fallback — the stated reason for the dual implementation — is inert for every user in Vim. No test covers Vim detection; the integration filetype probes run Neovim only.

## Fix

Use `set filetype=shellspec` (overrule) in the four ftdetect autocmds, which is the documented form for ftdetect rules that must override a generic detection. Add a Vim integration probe that asserts `&ft ==# 'shellspec'` for `x_spec.sh`.

## Resolution
ftdetect uses `set filetype=shellspec`; integration test asserts Vim sets shellspec for *_spec.sh; README/doc restore snippet corrected too.
title: ftdetect uses setfiletype, which loses to the built-in *.sh rule: spec files open as sh in Vim

body:
## Problem

`format_buffer_async(bufnr)` defaults `bufnr` to 0 and passes 0 into `vim.schedule` (format.lua:251-259); `:ShellSpecFormatAsync` calls it with no argument (autocmds.lua:62). Buffer 0 is resolved when the callback runs, not when the command was issued, so a buffer switch in between redirects the formatting to a different — possibly non-shellspec — buffer.

## Evidence

`vim.cmd('ShellSpecFormatAsync'); vim.cmd('edit other.py'); vim.wait(300)` with other.py = `def f():` / `        return 1`:

- other.py buffer afterwards: `['def f():', 'return 1']` — Python indentation destroyed.
- The spec buffer is left unformatted: `['Describe "x"', 'It "y"', 'End', 'End']`.

## Impact

A mapping or autocmd that runs the async command and then moves on (`:ShellSpecFormatAsync<CR>:bnext<CR>`) rewrites an unrelated file's indentation.

## Fix

Resolve the handle before scheduling: `if bufnr == nil or bufnr == 0 then bufnr = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() end`. Inside the callback, skip the call when `not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(bufnr)`. Add a unit test that schedules, switches buffers, and asserts only the original buffer changed.

## Resolution
format_buffer_async resolves 0/nil to the current buffer before scheduling and skips invalid buffers; unit Test 20 switches buffers and asserts only the original changed.
title: :ShellSpecFormatAsync resolves buffer 0 on the next tick and formats whichever buffer is current then

body:
## Problem

README.md:121 recommends `vim.keymap.set('v', '<leader>sf', '<cmd>ShellSpecFormatRange<cr>')`. A `<cmd>` mapping executes without inserting `'<,'>`, so the range command receives the default range (the cursor line), not the selection.

## Evidence

Unformatted 5-line spec, `VG` then the mapping:

- `<cmd>ShellSpecFormatRange<cr>` → file unchanged (only the last line, `End`, was formatted).
- The same selection with `':ShellSpecFormatRange<cr>'` → fully formatted (`  It "y"`, `    When call f`, `  End`).

## Impact

Users who copy the documented config get a visual-format key that silently does nothing useful.

## Fix

Change the README line to `vim.keymap.set('x', '<leader>sf', ':ShellSpecFormatRange<cr>', { desc = 'Format ShellSpec selection' })`.

## Resolution
README visual mapping is now `vim.keymap.set('x', '<leader>sf', ':ShellSpecFormatRange<cr>')`, with the reason in a comment.
title: README's visual-mode keymap uses <cmd>, which passes no range, so it formats only the cursor line

body:
## Problem

plugin/shellspec.vim:41 defines `command! -range ShellSpecFormatRange call shellspec#format_selection()`. The range is never passed, and `shellspec#format_selection` reads the `'<`/`'>` marks (autoload/shellspec.vim:166-167). An explicit `:2,4ShellSpecFormatRange` therefore formats the last visual selection, or nothing. Separately, `deletebufline('%', start, end)` followed by `append(start - 1, formatted)` (lines 175-176) leaves the one empty line Vim keeps when a buffer is emptied, so selecting every line adds a trailing blank line.

## Evidence

Vim 9 (`vim -N -e -s -u NONE`, fallback path):

- `:2,4ShellSpecFormatRange` on an unformatted file with no prior selection → file unchanged.
- `ggVG` then `:ShellSpecFormatRange` on a 4-line file → 5 lines, the last one empty (`End$` / `$`).

doc/shellspec.txt:66 documents `:{range}ShellSpecFormatRange`.

## Impact

The documented range form does not work in Vim, and formatting a whole-file selection modifies the file beyond indentation.

## Fix

Pass the range explicitly. `command! -range ShellSpecFormatRange call shellspec#format_selection(<line1>, <line2>)` with `function! shellspec#format_selection(start, end) abort` using `a:start`/`a:end` instead of the marks. Replace the delete+append with `call setline(a:start, l:formatted)`; line counts are equal, since format_lines never adds or removes lines. Add an integration test that runs `:2,4ShellSpecFormatRange` under Vim.

## Resolution
Fallback command passes <line1>,<line2>; shellspec#format_selection(start, end) uses setline in place. Integration test runs :1,$ShellSpecFormatRange under Vim and asserts content and line count.
title: Vim fallback :ShellSpecFormatRange ignores its range, and a whole-buffer selection gains a blank line

run_tests.sh and make test-unit run the suite via pcall(dofile) and `cquit 1` on error.

## Problem

`shellspecBlockLine` (syntax/shellspec.vim:51) is meant to host the `contained` `shellspecTag`. On a line starting at column 0, the `syn keyword shellspecBlock Describe ...` match begins at the same column, and a keyword beats a match that starts at the same position. The container therefore never starts and the tag stays unhighlighted. On indented lines the container starts at col 0 (the whitespace) and wins, but it spans to `$` and does not contain `shellspecComment`, so `It "x" # note` loses comment highlighting.

## Evidence

`synstack()` in Vim on `Describe "d" tag:one` col 14 → `[]`. On `  It "i" tag:two` col 16 → `['shellspecBlockLine', 'shellspecTag']`.

## Impact

The change's stated purpose (tags highlighted) holds only for nested blocks; top-level `Describe` tags remain plain, and the new region regresses trailing comments.

## Fix

Drop the container and make tags match only after a block keyword: `syn match shellspecTag "\%(^\s*[xf]\?\%(Describe\|Context\|ExampleGroup\|It\|Specify\|Example\)\>.*\)\@<=\<\w\+:\w\+\>"` (not `contained`). Delete `shellspecBlockLine`.

## Resolution
shellspecBlockLine container removed; shellspecTag is a top-level match with a block-keyword lookbehind. synstack confirms tags highlighted at column 0 and indented.
title: Tag highlighting fix does not apply to unindented block lines, and block lines hide trailing comments

## Problem

`trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' EXIT INT TERM` (bin/shellspec-format:308). A trap on INT/TERM that does not call `exit` makes bash resume after the handler, so the loop keeps writing to the unlinked temp file. The later `mv` then fails.

## Evidence

A 200,000-line spec formatted in place, SIGINT sent after 1 s → the process was still running 120 s later and had to be killed. No temp file remained (the handler removed it) and the original was unchanged.

## Impact

Ctrl-C does not interrupt the tool. It runs to completion and then fails with an `mv: cannot stat` error.

## Fix

Split the traps: `trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' EXIT` and `trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"; exit 130' INT; trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"; exit 143' TERM`. Clear all three after the `mv`, as now.

## Resolution
INT/TERM traps clean up and exit 130/143; verified SIGINT on a 200k-line in-place run exits 130 with the file unchanged and no temp left. No automated test (signal timing).
title: INT/TERM trap deletes the temp file but does not exit, so Ctrl-C does not stop in-place formatting
